SP-460's activation gate, under which a kind appends nothing until every family it needs is admitted, is outside the sequences; `family_not_admitted_quarantined` covers the quarantine of a family that is not admitted.
| `COLLAB-UNCERTAIN-01` | An uncertain append of a run's event | The run is fenced: no later event of that run appends until Storage resolves the original identity |
| `COLLAB-QUARANTINE-01` | An event of a family that is not admitted | Quarantined before append; no checkpoint advance; no sibling state inferred |
| `COLLAB-WITHDRAW-01` | Withdrawal of one admitted family | Writer cut off, current core withdrawn, readers fenced, governed rebuild from kept seglog records; no deletion |

**Admission order.** `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` admits one event at a time under the existing Storage append-writer lock: (1) **exact retry**: the dedupe identity `(scope_partition, event_type, idempotency_key)` with the same producer semantic digest returns the original event and result, its receipt only through `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`; the same identity with another digest is `idempotency_conflict` and appends nothing; (2) **family admission**: a type the registry does not admit, or an application edition still marked `requires_owner_adoption`, is quarantined before append and advances no checkpoint; (3) **payload**: the edition's CV-460 to CV-478 definition and the EventRecord joins; (4) **current projection**: the projector first brings the checkpoint up to the verified tail of the scope partition under the same lock, or the call returns `collaboration_projection_unavailable` and appends nothing; (5) **transition**: the family's own unit checks the event against the current rows and returns `collaboration_conflict` with one `conflict_kind` on refusal; (6) **append** through the ordinary EventRecord path with SP-336's single data sync for the group, then first-receipt custody.
A genuinely absent append may retry only that prepared semantic request; unresolved original custody keeps the run/definition fenced.
A run whose append is uncertain stays fenced until Storage resolves it.

Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile.
The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

A genuinely absent append may retry only that prepared semantic request; unresolved original custody keeps the run/definition fenced.
A run whose append is uncertain stays fenced until Storage resolves it.

First AppendReceipt follows committed group durability; approval/receipt barriers require full flush. Publish terminal result, progression or queue release only after the original receipt resolves. Uncertain append fences later subject work until resolution; missing receipt never authorizes a fresh identity or repeated external effect. Replay retrieves original source/result and never dispatches a tool, issues approval, recreates/deletes a worktree, enqueues work, charges usage or sends a notification. For approval.timeout, allocate the original source operation identity before any effect. Its idempotency_key is 'dt:' plus lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JSON [event_type, scope_partition, run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, approval_scope_key], preserving those exact source values. event_id is 'evt_dt_' plus SHA-256 of UTF-8 idempotency_key. Use dedupe_by_idempotency_key and the complete CV-EventRecord producer_semantic_digest; same identity/different semantic digest refuses idempotency_conflict. Retries retain occurred_at_utc and every source/envelope field. The operating consumer storage.dt.approval_timeout.reader.v1@1.0.0 serves HITL resolver, runtime blocked controls and inspection; it directly filters verified EventRecord index reads for this exact family, not an invented second domain database. It explicitly adopts SP-278 and DL-076's nine-field durable token, never persisted redb_snapshot_id. Checkpoint key projector.checkpoint.dt.approval_timeout:{storage_instance_id}:{scope_partition} stores Plans/dt_event_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/approval_timeout_checkpoint. Validate storage instance, partition, token generation/frontier/coverage/source selection and exact admitted family/version before publication. Empty source is proven by the source token, never guessed from no matches. Rebuild from verified retained source with recovery holds, never from checkpoint alone; source gaps return unavailable, never silently skip them. Canonical seglog originals and referenced bodies remain under mandatory coherent backup/restore, source access and deletion checks; opaque refs grant no access. Keep credentials, tool arguments, raw output and private file contents out of this payload; refs are opaque permission-checked locators, bounded reasons/previews are redacted before persistence. Backup restores original source, dedupe/receipt custody and references coherently or fences mutation; checkpoints rebuild, and an older restore never revives a resolved approval or deleted worktree. Unknown version refuses current mutation and disclosure until a validating reader/upgrader is installed; legacy aliases normalize before persistence only with original source proof, never by replay side effects. Withdrawal first cuts off this family's append admission, then fences its consumer/readers and marks checkpoint withdrawn with a fixed timestamp. No advance or ordinary read follows; governed compatible rebuild and revalidated source/admission are required to resume. No zero-cursor reset, sibling substitution or history rewrite. retention_policy_ref = RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE. The codec is pm.dt.source.json.v1 canonical UTF-8 JSON without BOM/newline, maximum 1048576 bytes per stage; reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, malformed Unicode, unknown fields and unsupported version. SHA-256 binds exact bytes; file paths are derived from the validated event_id and literal stage under this Storage instance, never caller paths. HITLBlockedEpisodeOwner.timeout owns preparation and authenticates HITLBlockedEpisodeOwner.timeout.resolve_original against the actual original human-in-the-loop.md owner_ref/revision, not the caller's witness or today's reconstructed configuration. Install the exact source schema/codec and append admission via StorageMigrationCoordinator, then validate current family admission, scope, actor and all family predicates before preparing or performing work. Publish prepared.json once under the subject owner lock using SP-131 same-directory temp/fsync/no-overwrite promotion and synchronized parent entries; allocate the original identity first. A byte-identical existing stage is reused; different bytes fence the subject. If it cannot prove original outcome, return unavailable and do not repeat any effect. completed.json is immutable, links prepared_sha256, carries the exact redacted closed payload and frozen envelope_context, and names the immutable owner_outcome_ref. Only then append the exact EventRecord; SP-286/CV-339 full-value v2 resolves the first eleven-field receipt, including its original seal-time timestamp. Source and completed payload/identity/envelope joins and current owner permissions/deletion are revalidated under the final owner lock after every helper. For this family require a barrier-class full flush through original outcome/source files, packs, segment commit frame and canonical receipt before terminal publication or authorizing dependent work. The nine-field durable token must equal the actual current generic-index capture (storage instance, root/node/dataset, generation anchor, frontier revision/hash and source_selection); reacquire the live redb snapshot without persisting its id. Capture complete global source coverage, source-frame verification and exact filter/version before evaluating any matching row. Under the source/maintenance fence and the exact consumer writer lease, recheck the entire old checkpoint value, current token, admission/installed-reader, permissions, tombstones and withdrawal; one redb transaction CASes the entire checkpoint. Failed CAS, changed frontier/source, missing retained prefix, future source version or any failed final guard publishes nothing and returns unavailable. Rows from any Project/application partition remain part of global examined coverage even when filtered out. Empty global source and a nonempty prefix with zero family matches are separate cases. Withdraw first cuts off new append admission under coordinator exclusion; drain admitted receipts, fence reader CAS and fix withdrawn_at_utc once. A withdrawn checkpoint cannot advance or disclose; reinstallation requires fresh governed source verification/rebuild, never zero reset. Rebuild reads retained canonical source and original source/receipt closures under recovery holds; at most three same-key generations, no source eviction from checkpoint pressure. Readers only inspect; recovery never performs a tool, approval, enqueue, notification, Settings or worktree action.
For approval.timeout alone, source codec pm.dt.source.json.v1 writes null/booleans as JSON literals, integers in exact shortest signed decimal (nonnegative source counters retain u64 without float conversion), finite fractional numbers as exact plain decimals with trailing fractional zeroes removed (no exponent and negative zero becomes zero), UTF-8 strings with JSON quote/backslash/control escaping and no Unicode normalization, arrays in order, and closed-object keys ordered by strict UTF-8 bytes. Duplicate keys, malformed Unicode, BOM, whitespace outside strings and nonfinite numbers are refused. Source decoder uses exact decimal parsing, not IEEE-754 conversion; a complete canonical-byte reencode must equal the input. This is a newly authored source-file codec, not a change to EventRecord's RFC 8785 semantic digest. For the identity preimage only, every unsigned integer subject is its shortest unsigned decimal string; thus all elements of the RFC 8785 array are strings. scope_partition is the existing Storage app or project~base64url(UTF-8 actual project_id without padding), never literal caller concatenation.
For approval.timeout, boolean authority/context flags are exact booleans before their value is evaluated. A prior checkpoint must validate before CAS/state comparisons. Prefix rows must be objects with owner-valid unsigned integer sequence ids and nonempty string event type, event id and scope partition before filtering. This type-safety rule changes no numeric spelling, integer range, physical bytes or retained-history recipe.
For approval.timeout alone, the explicit lifecycle transition is requested -> timed_out: actual original deadline expired; no authorization. prepared.before contains only original prerequisites known before the owner operation; completed.owner_result contains the closed authentic original outcome fields, which cannot be guessed at prepare time. The original owner commits those fields under the preallocated subject identity; payload outcome fields must equal that result. A completed source is accepted only with the exact prepare digest, original owner result and complete captured joins. No immutable prepared record is overwritten with a later outcome. Duplicate delivery returns the complete original receipt/value; invalid predecessors or changed prerequisites refuse without a new append or dependent publication. The named resolve_original method takes exactly storage_instance_id, scope_partition, event_id, idempotency_key, owner_ref and owner_revision; it returns exactly unavailable(reason_code) or original(prepared source, completed source, original full EventRecord, original eleven-field AppendReceipt or null before issuance). These records use this family's exact schemas and immutable files; the method authenticates actual owner transactions/files/permissions, never a caller assertion. Before issuance it may finalize from a provable original outcome and append only the frozen original; a missing or uncertain owner result remains unavailable/fenced.

This synthetic adapter is an explicit native-authentication assumption, not a claim that fixture booleans authenticate Storage frames. The source codec byte vectors, exact source/owner_result separation, application server/operation/codec negatives where applicable, independent lifecycle transitions, pending/known retention gates and held-generation capacity cases are executable static oracles in scripts/pm-dt-event-contracts.py. Each recovery/checkpoint fixture is also a concrete native crash/race obligation; original owner transaction, fsync, wire, permissions and redb CAS remain NOT_RUN.
For approval.timeout alone, the ordinary canonical append/read path adopts Case L-2, SP-026 and SP-236 SeglogFrameV2 without a family-specific wire decoder or new header. SP-337 owns the 16 KiB inline limit and BLAKE3 payload-pack addressing; a separately governed or larger payload is resolved through the actual permission-checked pack reader before schema/join validation. A pack body and its index are durable before the referencing group receipt; a missing, changed, unverified or deleted pack body is unavailable, never an empty successful result. claim_audit.text: **Replay, rebuild and withdrawal.** Replay runs in canonical seglog order from the checkpoint's inclusive cursor and only rebuilds projection rows: no message delivery, dispatch, card, notification, command or append follows from replay. Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

claim_audit.text: Newly authored owner contract under DL-090. Plans/collaboration_event_payloads.schema.json closes the payloads of the 18 collaborative workflow families, each with a project edition pm.collaboration_event.<token>.v1 and an application edition pm.collaboration_event.<token>.application.v1 at 1.0.0, selected by exact scope and schema ID. Every payload requires schema_version, scope_kind, project_id (null only in application scope), thread_id, collaboration_id, collaboration_run_id, kind, definition_revision, currentness_hash and idempotency_key, and application payloads server_id. Optional fields are omitted, never null. Closed sets reference Collaborative Workflows section 12's enumerations; reasons are section 11 codes other than cancelled. References use CV-353's non_secret_ref form. No payload carries user or participant text. The EventRecord joins fix scope, identity, run, attempt, schema, redaction, replay, occurrence time and the SP-460 identity recipe. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, received 2bda6aeed0): «Nothing is admitted». SP-337 externalizes bodies above 16384 canonical UTF-8 bytes and verifies complete resolved bytes and identical payload joins. Identifiers and hashes use true-end lexical guards. Family/envelope equality is mandatory; SP-460 defines lossless numeric serialization, exact control types and field-level frozen caller-envelope/source custody. CV-1100 governs current integer input, SP-1100 the Storage uint64 and physical profiles, SP-1101 retained-original recipe selection and CV-1101 each timestamp's owner profile. Four explicit collaborative app V2 wrappers independently fit 16384 MessagePack bytes or use verified SP-337 logical-record references; closed V1 definitions are preserved.

claim_audit.text:
browser.context_shared 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract, prepared without admission before the 2026-11-18 registration. This exact family independently adopts the following bindings, not a sibling's contract. Source: DL-433 landed in Plans/Decision_Log.md on origin/main, authored on origin/plans/ea-cards2-answers-20261105, presented deck item 4.c, SHA-256 6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30. Jared's words alone: "i approve all of it". The deck's fast-reply rule selects A; the option below is the card author's wording, not a Jared quotation.
Approved option A: Keep a separate sharing grant for each recipient chat. Sharing with another chat keeps earlier grants. Stop sharing with a named chat removes only that grant; Stop sharing without a chat removes every grant for the selected browser session. Sharing itself never copies page contents into chat.
Card **Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:830-831`; `MAIN:Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:843-846`; `DS15:reports/event-authority-20261104/DS15.md:91-94`; `evidence:reviews/DS15-sol/REVIEW.md:55-61`; `evidence:reviews/DS15-sol/REVIEW-cycle4.md:99-104`; `evidence:reviews/DS15-sol/REVIEW-cycle5.md:203-218`.
Search: /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/drafts/DS15/r9/browser_context_shared-search.json; scope current top-level Plans Markdown/JSON and scripts Python at 30dc9245bc753dbe80693977a1b03e3278d73b85, excluding source ledgers/generated artifacts. Required behavior exists; no complete exact-family technical binding was found. DL-045 permits newly authored technical bindings; DL-433 resolves only the stated behavior choice. Reuse SP-278/SP-286/CV-339/CV-366/SP-337 and actual existing command/Doctor owner outcomes.
Producer: Browser session sharing controller for cmd.browser.share_with_agent commits one recipient-chat grant. The resolved recipient must have the same actual subject scope. Preserve every prior grant, including grants to other chats. There is one grant per recipient chat; an already-held grant retains its existing grant identity. This records sharing authority only; no page body, screenshot, DOM, selection, capture chip, message send or browser.context_captured effect follows.
Scope and identity: actual Project or application namespace selected by the owning component, never current focus, time or a fabricated Project. This family has scope_policy=application_or_project. Original event_id is allocated once and retained. Idempotency recipe: application scope: application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; Project scope: sha256(canonical MessagePack array ["browser.context_shared", "1.0.0", actual scope map with UTF-8 sorted keys, operation_id]). Application server_id and original_operation_id resolve from the immutable owner operation source; Project partition is encoded project~base64url, app partition is app. scope_key is SHA-256 of the canonical MessagePack scope map in UTF-8 key order. Retried caller-supplied CV-317 semantic body must equal the original; Storage-assigned sequence and timestamps are excluded from retry comparison and independently authenticated by full-value original custody.
Closed payload: Plans/ds15_browser_context_shared.schema.json; closed original transition/source schemas: Plans/ds15_deck2_context.schema.json and Plans/ds15_deck2_sources.schema.json, own definitions by exact event name. No raw content, credentials, file paths, executable/configuration bodies, cookies, captures or provider data. All string identifiers/ref fields fully match their schema at the real boundary, including LF refusal. Numbers (sweep 2026-11-08): current inputs follow CV-1100 and SP-1100: raw JSON through loads_current_json, current_integer at every schema integer slot with that slot's own bounds, storage_uint64 for Storage sequence, generation and offset metadata, storage_value_bytes(EVENT_VALUE) for inline-size and identity-preimage bytes, full_value_commitment for CV-339 and the qualified JCS of the CV-317 projection, owner integer paths type-sensitive, before a new append. Retained originals keep the frozen ds15-v1 profile they were written under, selected only through SP-1101 (sweep 2026-11-11): a retained reader or retry resolver first takes one selection from the one write receipt Storage sealed with that exact original (its Storage instance, original ref and CV-339 commitment), never from the Storage instance or family alone, where no custody or no receipt is the existing unavailable contract and more than one receipt or an uninstalled recipe is unsupported, never a fallback to the current or another recipe, and a new append takes the writer's own recipe without reading a receipt; it then resolves the original once through the shared RetainedDispatcher, whose sealed owner authenticates the fetched bytes by their CV-339 commitment and whose frozen verifier recomputes the original, so a coherently rewritten original refuses. Timestamps follow CV-1101 through the shared predicate: every format: date-time takes the EventRecord profile and the Storage-assigned EventRecord observed and persisted times take CV-253's storage_utc_z, for current inputs and retained originals alike; a skipped past format check authorizes no history. No new cap, number codec or date-time grammar is introduced. SP-337 resolves bodies over the 16384-byte inline boundary by original owner payload references; this bounded metadata schema grants no oversized-inline exception. Measure complete encoded envelope payload and checkpoint.
Original source and custody: outcome_ref resolves independently retained owning-component record bytes, never a caller's matching assertion. Reparse and validate the closed exact-family source; join original payload, event_type, scope, Storage instance, original operation identity and original transition observations field by field. The source bank in static fixtures models this owner resolver, not a new production database. Adopt SP-286 / CV-339 full-value original/first-AppendReceipt custody. Commit original transition/source, freeze event, single-writer append/dedupe, retain first receipt and full-value commitment, then publish. Missing original, incoherent closure or unavailable source blocks publication/recovery. Backup/restore preserves original source/log/receipt/consumption closure together. Current authorization, Project/chat permissions, deletion/redaction and sharing withdrawal are rechecked on read; a checkpoint grants no access.
Replay and transitions: retry/lost acknowledgement returns original event_id, immutable outcome and first receipt with zero repeated effects. Recover a missing append with original identity only; never regrant, revoke again, update, remove or issue another notice. Current writer/retry refuses projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable; retained supported 1.0.0 replay-only originals remain readable after authenticating their original transition and source, whatever today's live state. Retained history never requires a disposed current transition control; current disclosure/access/deletion and withdrawal still fence it. Ordinary replay dispatches no command.
Consumer and checkpoint: reader.ds15.browser_context_shared.v1@1.0.0 is the exact operating browser.context_shared history reader and reads only browser.context_shared@1.0.0. Adopt SP-278 and DL-076 nine-field durable read token; key projector.checkpoint.ds15.browser_context_shared:{scope_key}, closed value Plans/ds15_browser_context_shared_checkpoint.schema.json. Physical proposed value: derived redb, coordination_and_storage budget, messagepack_canonical, full encoded value at most 16384 bytes (SP-339/SP-340). This task appends no storage-value registry row and authorizes no physical write/advance. Capture CURRENT-selected complete global range and live snapshot; persist only the nine-field token, never redb_snapshot_id. Scan every global row, resolve each matching original, join event id/type/scope/partition/Storage sequence. Advance by atomic CAS of complete prior and new checkpoint in one redb transaction. Missing rows, contradictions, mismatched token/Storage/snapshot/source, changed access or reader version preserve prior. through_sequence_id is the global scanned frontier and last_event_id the last verified match; no checkpoint before first match, a zero-match suffix keeps the earlier last event. Rebuild requires complete retained prefix and fresh permissions.
Retention: Event retention adopts DL-401 G10 / RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0 from the landed Plans/Decision_Log.md entry on origin/main: the payload thread_id is the governing recipient chat, including No project. At most 250000 per chat then linked successor; no records dropped, holds and chat deletion deadlines apply. The policy object is on Plans/storage_value_registry.json's retention_policies list. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Checkpoint retention_policy_ref=PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION.» Exact question: What retention and deletion rule governs the scope-wide browser.context_shared reader checkpoint when its source events belong to different recipient chats? Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Current chat permissions and deletion fences apply even while this assignment is pending.» Retention premise evidence is DL-401 and G10/G11/G14 as named for this exact family in Plans/storage-plan.md, landed on origin/main; those lines are byte-identical at origin/plans/ea-retention-cards2-20261105 commit 9b76338594c6f1ca75de6c757e7a8b98ab68e229; none of items 4.c-4.f changes that grouping. Referenced content follows its own independently approved lifetime, redaction and read access.
Compatibility and withdrawal: exact 1.0.0 writer/reader/schema only. Unknown version/field fails closed. Writer withdrawal uses committed admission frontier, refuses new admissions and drains only already-admitted original outcomes/receipts; reader withdrawal fences CAS and marks checkpoints withdrawn. Reinstallation needs current authorization and a complete retained-source rebuild. No fabricated old recipe selector; shared number/format historical-selector defects remain explicit sweep work.
Oracles: ATS-329's exact browser.context_shared section, Plans/ds15_deck2_fixtures.json own family row, and python3 scripts/pm-ds15-deck2-contracts.py --family browser.context_shared. Each negative has one declared defect and explicit coherent derived observations; fixture source/custody joins are verified against actual retained values. Native execution NOT_RUN. At preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, registry membership was ABSENT; preparation itself granted no admission, new feature, Decision Log entry or readiness claim.

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `document_generation_committed`: A document change advances the page generation and invalidates prior representation identities. `cmd.browser.page.evaluate` emits it under its existing binding: "Conditional on the permitted named action actually changing navigation/document generation; read-only/no-change actions return their owner result without either event.". The outcomes `pre_dispatch_rejection`, `handler_unavailable`, `acceptance_only`, `no_change` are event-silent. Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is not Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are both null or both the verified initiating lineage, never fabricated to obtain an expiry. claim_audit.text: **Append.** The ordinary EventRecord append (Case L-5) accepts this family only once the registry admits it; until then it returns `missing_event_registration` with no append, receipt or checkpoint. Checks run in this order: registry admission, then the writer cutoff (a withdrawn family refuses `family_withdrawn` even for a same-key retry), then dedupe catch-up to the log tail (`dedupe_unavailable`), then the CV-2509 envelope, body, identity and the producer's resolved owner transition, then the append. `storage.first_append_receipt.issue.v2` issues the eleven-field first receipt; the custody v2 row joins the event ID, Storage's `scope_partition`, event type, idempotency key, producer-semantic digest, the shared full-value commitment and every receipt field to Storage's own record, with `durability_state=synced` and `acknowledged_at_utc` on the EventRecord profile. Success is reported only when that synced receipt exists for this event; an uncertain append reports nothing. A lost-ack retry returns the original receipt from `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`, appends no second record and assigns no new sequence; a changed semantic digest refuses `idempotency_conflict`.

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `page_closed`: The exact page is closed and its mutation authority is no longer usable. `cmd.browser.page.close` emits it under its existing binding: "Only after the exact page closes; no newest/focused-page substitution.". The outcomes `pre_dispatch_rejection`, `handler_unavailable`, `acceptance_only`, `no_change` are event-silent. Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is not Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are both null or both the verified initiating lineage, never fabricated to obtain an expiry. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); prior_page_generation is null or at most page_generation (`generation_not_regressed`, GS10).

Compiler, segment, workspace, lease, routing and timeout subevents use their individually admitted owner rows; they are not new GUI commands.". Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. Checks run in this order: registry admission, then the writer cutoff (a withdrawn family refuses `family_withdrawn` even for a same-key retry), then dedupe catch-up to the log tail (`dedupe_unavailable`), then the CV-2522 envelope, body, identity and the producer's resolved owner transition, then the append. `storage.first_append_receipt.issue.v2` issues the eleven-field first receipt; the custody v2 row joins the event ID, Storage's `scope_partition`, event type, idempotency key, producer-semantic digest, the shared full-value commitment and every receipt field to Storage's own record, with `durability_state=synced` and `acknowledged_at_utc` on the EventRecord profile. Success is reported only when that synced receipt exists for this event; an uncertain append reports nothing. A lost-ack retry returns the original receipt from `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`, appends no second record and assigns no new sequence; a changed semantic digest refuses `idempotency_conflict`.

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `program_resumed_revalidated`: The same program resumes only after current checkpoint, permission, target, and generation revalidation. `cmd.browser.program.resume` emits it under its existing binding: "Only after current checkpoint, Run/Attempt, generation, lease, permission and target revalidation.". The outcomes `pre_dispatch_rejection`, `handler_unavailable`, `acceptance_only`, `no_change` are event-silent. Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are the actual Run and Attempt of the program execution, never fabricated, as SMPFS-166 requires for programs, compilation, segments and ProgramWorkspace. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); result_workspace_revision is at least expected_workspace_revision (`workspace_revision_not_regressed`, GS28); checkpoint_ref is a non-empty reference (`checkpoint_ref_present`, GS29); no action id is both completed and unknown-effect (`no_action_overlap`, GS30); effect_state effect_unknown forbids retry_allowed (`unknown_state_no_retry`, GS31); unknown-effect actions forbid retry_allowed (`unknown_actions_no_retry`, GS32); effect_state no_effect has no unknown-effect actions (`no_effect_no_unknown`, GS33); effect_state no_effect has no completed actions (`no_effect_no_completed`, GS34).

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `segment_checkpoint_committed`: A segment checkpoint commits its effect/workspace boundary and continuation reference. No catalogue command emits it; it is an internal segment transition of the owner and needs no invented GUI command (SMPFS-166). Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are the actual Run and Attempt of the program execution, never fabricated, as SMPFS-166 requires for programs, compilation, segments and ProgramWorkspace. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); result_workspace_revision is at least expected_workspace_revision (`workspace_revision_not_regressed`, GS28); checkpoint_ref is a non-empty reference (`checkpoint_ref_present`, GS29); no action id is both completed and unknown-effect (`no_action_overlap`, GS30); effect_state effect_unknown forbids retry_allowed (`unknown_state_no_retry`, GS31); unknown-effect actions forbid retry_allowed (`unknown_actions_no_retry`, GS32); effect_state no_effect has no unknown-effect actions (`no_effect_no_unknown`, GS33); effect_state no_effect has no completed actions (`no_effect_no_completed`, GS34).

claim_audit.text: **Append.** The ordinary EventRecord append (Case L-5) accepts this family only once the registry admits it; until then it returns `missing_event_registration` with no append, receipt or checkpoint. Checks run in this order: registry admission, then the writer cutoff (a withdrawn family refuses `family_withdrawn` even for a same-key retry), then dedupe catch-up to the log tail (`dedupe_unavailable`), then the CV-2528 envelope, body, identity and the producer's resolved owner transition, then the append. `storage.first_append_receipt.issue.v2` issues the eleven-field first receipt; the custody v2 row joins the event ID, Storage's `scope_partition`, event type, idempotency key, producer-semantic digest, the shared full-value commitment and every receipt field to Storage's own record, with `durability_state=synced` and `acknowledged_at_utc` on the EventRecord profile. Success is reported only when that synced receipt exists for this event; an uncertain append reports nothing. A lost-ack retry returns the original receipt from `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`, appends no second record and assigns no new sequence; a changed semantic digest refuses `idempotency_conflict`.

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `segment_failed_disposed`: The segment fails with typed no-effect or reconciled-effect disposition and retry safety. No catalogue command emits it; it is an internal segment transition of the owner and needs no invented GUI command (SMPFS-166). Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are the actual Run and Attempt of the program execution, never fabricated, as SMPFS-166 requires for programs, compilation, segments and ProgramWorkspace. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); result_workspace_revision is at least expected_workspace_revision (`workspace_revision_not_regressed`, GS28); no action id is both completed and unknown-effect (`no_action_overlap`, GS30); effect_state effect_unknown forbids retry_allowed (`unknown_state_no_retry`, GS31); unknown-effect actions forbid retry_allowed (`unknown_actions_no_retry`, GS32); effect_state no_effect has no unknown-effect actions (`no_effect_no_unknown`, GS33); effect_state no_effect has no completed actions (`no_effect_no_completed`, GS34); terminal_state failed_no_effect requires effect_state no_effect (`failed_no_effect_state`, GS35); any other terminal_state has no unknown-effect actions (`terminal_no_unknown_actions`, GS37); any other terminal_state has a known effect_state (`terminal_known_state`, GS38).

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `timeout_effects_reconciled`: Timeout effects are explicitly reconciled before any policy permits a retry. No catalogue command emits it; it is an internal program transition of the owner and needs no invented GUI command (SMPFS-166). Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are the actual Run and Attempt of the program execution, never fabricated, as SMPFS-166 requires for programs, compilation, segments and ProgramWorkspace. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); result_workspace_revision is at least expected_workspace_revision (`workspace_revision_not_regressed`, GS28); no action id is both completed and unknown-effect (`no_action_overlap`, GS30); effect_state effect_unknown forbids retry_allowed (`unknown_state_no_retry`, GS31); unknown-effect actions forbid retry_allowed (`unknown_actions_no_retry`, GS32); effect_state no_effect has no unknown-effect actions (`no_effect_no_unknown`, GS33); effect_state no_effect has no completed actions (`no_effect_no_completed`, GS34); any other terminal_state has no unknown-effect actions (`terminal_no_unknown_actions`, GS37); any other terminal_state has a known effect_state (`terminal_known_state`, GS38).

claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `program_workspace_spilled`: Large typed values spill through authorized artifact/storage ownership with bounded references. No catalogue command emits it; it is an internal program_workspace transition of the owner and needs no invented GUI command (SMPFS-166). Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are the actual Run and Attempt of the program execution, never fabricated, as SMPFS-166 requires for programs, compilation, segments and ProgramWorkspace. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04); result_workspace_revision is at least expected_workspace_revision (`workspace_revision_not_regressed`, GS28).

claim_audit.text: **Append.** The ordinary EventRecord append (Case L-5) accepts this family only once the registry admits it; until then it returns `missing_event_registration` with no append, receipt or checkpoint. Success is reported only when that synced receipt exists for this event; an uncertain append reports nothing. A lost-ack retry returns the original receipt from `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`, appends no second record and assigns no new sequence; a changed semantic digest refuses `idempotency_conflict`.

Success is reported only when that synced receipt exists for this event; an uncertain append reports nothing. claim_audit.text: **Transition.** The entitling owner transition is `fetch_route_selected`: Public static content selects the authorized Search/Fetch/Site Reader route before browser escalation. No catalogue command emits it; it is an internal routing transition of the owner and needs no invented GUI command (SMPFS-166). Only a transition the owner has committed emits; a pending, rejected, unavailable, acceptance-only or no-change outcome appends nothing, and an uncertain append is unresolved, never evidence of zero append. It is not Run-bound: `run_id` and `attempt_id` are both null or both the verified initiating lineage, never fabricated to obtain an expiry. The closed payload's family predicates, each enforced by the shared Browser owner validator and by its own s4b checker row: run_id and attempt_id are both null or both non-null (`run_attempt_paired`, GS01); browser_session_id and browser_workspace_id are both null or both non-null (`session_workspace_paired`, GS02); browser_page_id and page_generation are both null or both non-null (`page_generation_paired`, GS03); a non-null browser_page_id has a non-null browser_workspace_id (`page_has_workspace`, GS04).

claim_audit.text:
Newly authored owner contract for bsd.advice_emitted, prepared without admission before the 2026-11-18 registration under deck-2 item 9.a A. This exact name is required by section 19/BSD-020 and has no existing alias/admitted event contract in the per-name search recorded in reports/event-authority-20261105/W3D.md.
1 membership/version: at preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, registry membership was ABSENT. Proposed 1.0.0 payload is Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/advice_emitted; SP-318 and the central registry refuse writers only when the exact current registration is absent or another existing admission check fails.
2 owner: Back_Seat_Driver is the semantic owner; CV-1350 binds the closed payload/identity and SP-1350 binds proposed Storage values. Reuse BSD-006, BSD-009, BSD-031, BSD-032 rather than sibling definitions.
3 producer: BackSeatDriverService::deliver_advice owns this transition. The actual command/dispatch/provider/deadline source must be independently authenticated. Admission checks exact family/version, original operation and current owner/epoch/permission/Stop gates before effect. It commits the immutable selected lifecycle source and pending_event operation under owner CAS; body/payload packs are durable before references. Pending source wrappers and operation commit together under the original transition CAS; the owning lifecycle head remains at its prior committed state until original append custody is resolved and the complete operation/head publish together. A failed append cannot expose uncommitted advice or a fabricated success. Once actual admission exists, known BSD failure/quarantine isolation releases waiters through the existing owner path while Storage failure remains disclosed; this event never authorizes withholding the primary past its own bounded catch-up rule. Append the frozen producer input once, adopt SP-286/CV-339 by name including full-value stored v2 original resolution and SP-336/SP-347 durability. This prepared family selects durability_class=barrier because its canonical lifecycle/control transition and recovery result depend on the original receipt; no primary/external action is authorized by it. Expose no successful append result, event-dependent projection or provider dispatch before the genuine first AppendReceipt. Persist complete operation/result with that original receipt before terminal publication. A crash after body but before append resumes the frozen pending event; a crash after append resolves original custody before completing. Prior domain authorization is never inferred from this historical event. Missing registration means no append and existing missing_event_registration; dependent commands remain disabled.
4 payload: independently closed schema Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/advice_emitted, ref-only source bodies, exact tags, no raw protected content.
5 scope/identity: project_only and exact original source/assignment/binding/run/epoch/generation/actor/account joins are defined independently for this event in CV-1350. Never borrow another family's recipe.
6 replay/idempotency: same original identity and semantic bytes returns exactly the original result; a different semantic digest conflicts, missing tail-current authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable, and a missing original receipt/body stays unavailable. A current append/retry with projector_replay_only is replay_only_not_appendable. Historical reads/rebuilds do not dispatch a review/tool, charge Usage, insert another transcript note, notify, mutate canonical lifecycle state or create an event.
7 retention: retention_policy_ref={registry_schema_id: pm.storage_value_registry.v2, policy_id: RP-RUNTIME-365D, policy_version: 1.0.0}. This exact family belongs to the actual primary_run_id from its assignment (BSD section 16); its recorded run completion starts the 365-day clock, with 1,000,000/run and 5,000,000/project and linked successor compaction. A nonterminal/missing completion never fabricates an anchor. This is Storage Case L-3's Runtime/run/node/attempt class, not an extension of Card-1 G13's five computer-use names. Holds, latest-25-run/recovery/live-reference/backup protection and owner deletion rules still override expiry; replay/retry/restore never restart the clock. Operation-receipt custody follows the existing lifetime identity guarantee RP-EVENT-IDENTITY-APPROOT; rebuildable projections/checkpoints use RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and cannot outlive/read a source without verified custody. These technical rows do not extend linked private-transcript/content lifetime.
8 custody: the original BSD lifecycle source stays canonical under its pending physical family; the proposed operation stores only redacted refs, original identity, semantic commitment and exact first receipt. SP-337 externalizes oversized bodies and every stored value is separately measured at 16 KiB. Storage holds the original first receipt/full-value commitment; coherent backup/restore includes the actual lifecycle source, operation, payload packs, original receipt and controls. Every current read/retry/replay/restore validates original custody and present access/deletion/withdrawal. Raw retained quarantine output and the advisor private transcript are never rendered by the event reader. Deleted bodies stay unavailable; retained metadata is not permission to recreate content.
9 transitions: Records one accepted advice delivery at the eligible step boundary, after the finding decision is committed; it is not a second review result. The selected finding is emitted, with one stamped presentation_weight and one delivery for its review cycle. A reconfirmed finding cites the newer evidence; frozen_boundary requires the actual recorded synchronous frozen safe point. async_nit is nit at a nonterminal next-step boundary. terminal_timeout_stale requires a critical held finding, actual expired/released terminal catch-up, stale=true, unreconfirmed=true and note weight. All other deliveries have both markers false. Nit and cooldown-routed deliveries stamp aside; other deliveries stamp note. A reload never re-weights the note. No primary result, gate, or run state changes.
10 consumers/checkpoints: projector.bsd.advice_emitted@1.0.0, reader.bsd.advice_emitted@1.0.0 and operating consumer AssistantChat::bsd_advisor_note adopt SP-278 by name via SP-1350. They filter exactly bsd.advice_emitted, the actual Project partition and exact supported payload/version. A derived projection references the authentic original event/source state; it does not become canonical assignment/finding/policy state. Checkpoint and all changed projection rows advance atomically by exact prior-value CAS after complete scanned-range proof. Persist only the nine-field durable token; the current read transaction supplies redb_snapshot_id transiently. No GUI-local state, matching-row maximum or caller proof flag supplies currentness.
11 compatibility/withdrawal: There is no earlier admitted BSD event version to migrate or synthesize. The existing completed-review bsd_runtime_record is not this event and never expands into lifecycle history. Genuine future retained 1.0.0 originals remain inspectable under authenticated original admission and recipe after live epoch/config changes, including compatibility-only replay policy; unsupported/missing/substituted custody or withdrawn sources refuse. A writer cutoff first fences new owner operations and drains/resolves previously issued pending inputs, records the exact cutoff under Storage governance, then withdraws the selector. Readers stop on withdrawal, invalidate their publication/checkpoint and rebuild only under an explicitly admitted successor; no fallback aliases, silent migration or fresh effects. Rebuild discards only derived rows, preserves canonical original bytes and reports unavailable expired/lost source rather than claiming empty/success.
12 oracle plan: ATS-1230 and Plans/bsd_event_oracle_plan.json enumerate this exact family's valid paths and one-defect negatives, and scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_events.py executes them (phase 2 and PNC-019 lane s4d, 2026-11-14). Every refusal is one named single-predicate row of a generated Method B guard table of at most eight rows (scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_table_*.py), proved by the gated scripts/pm_guard_isolation.py; a row no input can refuse first sits alone in its own table with a written proof. Every payload field joins its authentic owner source and every payload reference resolves an owner-held object of its kind, subject and Project; the stored logical body joins the same source. Producer crash cuts, lost-acknowledgement retry, no-effect replay, governed withdrawal, successor rebuild, coherent backup restore and the bound retention policy run as behavioural models whose computed outcomes the rows observe. scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_derivation_mutations.py weakens every derivation clause and counts only an accepted witness as a kill; scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_slot_corpus.py runs the shared number and date-time corpus through every integer and timestamp slot; reports/event-authority-20261105/W3D-plan-coverage.json maps each plan entry to its executed rows and witnesses. This is synthetic oracle evidence: writer admission and registry membership were ABSENT during preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration; native execution remains NOT_RUN.
Current membership (2026-11-18) — bsd.advice_emitted@1.0.0 is individually registered in Plans/event_family_registry.json. Missing-registration refusal applies only if the exact current family/version/scope registration is absent; this registered family is not refused as missing_event_registration or family_not_admitted merely because it was prepared without admission. Append and checkpoint advance still require every existing schema, scope, retention, original-source, receipt, permission and withdrawal check specified here. Registry membership supplies no native execution proof or additional action authority.

claim_audit.active_text: Deck-2 item 9.a A (answer record 2026-11-05; DL-450 application pending)

claim_audit.text:
Newly authored owner contract, prepared without admission under deck-2 9.a A.
Newly authored identity for bsd.advice_emitted: project_only, family_revision=1.0.0, payload_schema_ref=Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/advice_emitted. CV-317/Contracts_V0 section 1.2 owns the complete EventRecord envelope; this unit defines no alternate envelope. project_id equals the original policy/binding Project; assignment-backed payloads join actual primary_run_id to envelope run_id, plus original thread/account/actor/causation values. A configuration-only event has run_id/assignment/epoch/generation null and never invents them. The original trusted operation selects owner_operation_id, from the accepted command_instance_id (manual actions), actual workflow-start dispatch identity (assignment/binding start), actual provider review-result identity (finding/failure/quarantine), or actual owner lifecycle/deadline identity (stop/timeout); a source transition component and the exact subject identity are appended as hex(UTF-8) components to distinguish separate transitions. The canonical operation ID is bsd-op@1:<hex(original_source_id)>:<hex(transition_component)>:<hex(subject_id)>; every component is an exact string from the authentic original source, never a caller assertion or retry clock. This family uses transition_component=bsd.advice_emitted and subject_id=bsd_finding_id. For multiple decisions about one subject within a review, original_source_id includes that owner decision identity, not merely the review cycle. Recompute from the original source. hex is lowercase byte hex of exact UTF-8, without trimming or normalization. event_id=bsd-event@1:<hex(actual_storage_instance_id)>:<hex(event_type)>:<hex(project_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>; idempotency_key=bsd-key@1:<hex(project_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>. Distinct fields are separated by literal colon and encoded components contain no colon. Use Storage's project~base64url partition and dedupe_by_idempotency_key. The app-root-global ID and lifetime scoped tuple are the envelope owner's identities; application is not admitted here. A future independently authorized application edition must use CV-366 application@1:<hex(server_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>, not this Project recipe. No operation is reminted by retry, restored focus or changed current epoch. SP-1365 defines the pending original-source wrappers; source_state_ref names the exact immutable source wrapper for this operation and its body is validated under the existing logical BSD schema. Binding, assignment, review and finding references resolve those exact owner objects, including their project/run/epoch joins, not merely matching labels. Every other non-constant payload field equals its authentic owner source (the accepted owner decision, the stored logical source body, the immutable review start, the canonical operation or the Project scope), and every payload reference resolves an owner-held object of that field's kind, this subject and this Project before use; the stored logical body's own identity fields join the same authentic source. Producer semantic digest is exactly the envelope-owner RFC8785/SHA-256 projection, excluding Storage-assigned sequence_id/observed_at_utc/persisted_at_utc. This family adopts by name the shared CV-1100/SP-1100 number rules (current_integer, storage_uint64, producer_semantic_digest, qualified_jcs, storage_value_bytes and full_value_commitment), the CV-1101 date-time profiles (event_record for occurred_at_utc and AppendReceipt acknowledged_at_utc, storage_utc_z for observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc, event_record for logical-body timestamps) and SP-1101 sealed-receipt retained-recipe dispatch (RetainedDispatcher); it defines no local number, timestamp or recipe code. finding_key is recomputed from the actual owner evidence, not accepted as supplied. SP-1365 requires an immutable, authenticated identity_inputs_ref for the finding source wrapper, resolving the closed finding_identity_inputs definition in Plans/bsd_event_storage_contracts.schema.json. It preserves the actual original source, finding_family classification string, affected/rule refs and evidence-owner fingerprint/source before any key is computed. Those operands are captured from the genuine original BSD decision, never inferred from a stored key or reconstructed from a later claim. The newly authored string-only recipe is bsd-finding@1:lowerhex(SHA256(RFC8785([normalized_family, sorted_exact_affected_refs, sorted_exact_rule_refs, evidence_fingerprint]))). Normalize the owner finding-family string by Unicode NFKC, Unicode lowercase, collapse each maximal non-letter/non-number run to underscore, trim underscores; arrays are deduplicated and sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes; reference strings themselves remain exact. The evidence fingerprint is the evidence owner's verified original commitment, never a new lane-local numeric digest. Genuine changed evidence yields a distinct key; unchanged closures and original identities remain immutable.
Payload Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/advice_emitted is an individually closed root (additionalProperties=false); all required/null/value/type branches and refs must be validated eagerly. Identifiers preserve exact owner strings, with LF/CR forbidden explicitly; digests have exact lengths. Every source reference is a typed opaque locator and still requires original custody, schema/version, source identity and access validation; a matching string or digest is never source authority. The event stores metadata and redacted refs, never policy instructions, finding claim bodies, advisor transcript or quarantine raw output. Retained record validation uses its authenticated original schema/recipe/admission; it does not pass through these current-write type/format/epoch tests. SP-337 externalizes the referenced source bodies. This EventRecord 2.0.0 family keeps its closed payload inline (payload_ref null): only the EventRecord 3.0.0 successor materializes the SP-337 event-payload reference route and this family has not adopted it, so an inline payload above 16 KiB is refused, never externalized. projector_replay_only is a historical-reader route and is refused by a current append/retry. No family membership or writer selector is added.

Append the frozen producer input once, adopt SP-286/CV-339 by name including full-value stored v2 original resolution and SP-336/SP-347 durability. This prepared family selects durability_class=barrier because its canonical lifecycle/control transition and recovery result depend on the original receipt; no primary/external action is authorized by it. Expose no successful append result, event-dependent projection or provider dispatch before the genuine first AppendReceipt. Persist complete operation/result with that original receipt before terminal publication. A crash after body but before append resumes the frozen pending event; a crash after append resolves original custody before completing. claim_audit.text:
Newly authored owner contract for bsd.workflow_binding_created, prepared without admission before the 2026-11-18 registration under deck-2 item 9.a A. This exact name is required by section 19/BSD-020 and has no existing alias/admitted event contract in the per-name search recorded in reports/event-authority-20261105/W3D.md.
1 membership/version: at preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, registry membership was ABSENT. Proposed 1.0.0 payload is Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/workflow_binding_created; SP-318 and the central registry refuse writers only when the exact current registration is absent or another existing admission check fails.
2 owner: Back_Seat_Driver is the semantic owner; CV-1364 binds the closed payload/identity and SP-1364 binds proposed Storage values. Reuse BSD-016, BSD-017, BSD-029 rather than sibling definitions.
3 producer: BackSeatDriverService::commit_workflow_binding_revision owns this transition. The actual command/dispatch/provider/deadline source must be independently authenticated. Admission checks exact family/version, original operation and current owner/epoch/permission/Stop gates before effect. It commits the immutable selected lifecycle source and pending_event operation under owner CAS; body/payload packs are durable before references. Pending source wrappers and operation commit together under the original transition CAS; the owning lifecycle head remains at its prior committed state until original append custody is resolved and the complete operation/head publish together. A failed append cannot expose uncommitted advice or a fabricated success. Once actual admission exists, known BSD failure/quarantine isolation releases waiters through the existing owner path while Storage failure remains disclosed; this event never authorizes withholding the primary past its own bounded catch-up rule. Append the frozen producer input once, adopt SP-286/CV-339 by name including full-value stored v2 original resolution and SP-336/SP-347 durability. This prepared family selects durability_class=barrier because its canonical lifecycle/control transition and recovery result depend on the original receipt; no primary/external action is authorized by it. Expose no successful append result, event-dependent projection or provider dispatch before the genuine first AppendReceipt. Persist complete operation/result with that original receipt before terminal publication. A crash after body but before append resumes the frozen pending event; a crash after append resolves original custody before completing. Prior domain authorization is never inferred from this historical event. Missing registration means no append and existing missing_event_registration; dependent commands remain disabled.
4 payload: independently closed schema Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/workflow_binding_created, ref-only source bodies, exact tags, no raw protected content.
5 scope/identity: project_only and exact original source/assignment/binding/run/epoch/generation/actor/account joins are defined independently for this event in CV-1364. Never borrow another family's recipe.
6 replay/idempotency: same original identity and semantic bytes returns exactly the original result; a different semantic digest conflicts, missing tail-current authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable, and a missing original receipt/body stays unavailable. A current append/retry with projector_replay_only is replay_only_not_appendable. Historical reads/rebuilds do not dispatch a review/tool, charge Usage, insert another transcript note, notify, mutate canonical lifecycle state or create an event.
7 retention: retention_policy_ref={registry_schema_id: pm.storage_value_registry.v2, policy_id: RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE, policy_version: 1.0.0}. DL-453 item 1.a (Back Seat Driver, Project editions only) assigns the saved frozen workflow-binding revision history to RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE@1.0.0 (Plans/storage-plan.md:17638,17642 at main f8b2098608): no age or count expiry and no new count allowance; the history stays inspectable subject to current access and explicit Delete Puppet Master project data (Remove project from list does not delete it); finite disk budgets still apply and refuse new records under pressure rather than evicting protected history. RP-CONFIG-CURRENT still governs the current configuration value, not this event history. Never infer approval/receipt authority from the companion operation receipt. Operation-receipt custody follows the existing lifetime identity guarantee RP-EVENT-IDENTITY-APPROOT; rebuildable projections/checkpoints use RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and cannot outlive/read a source without verified custody. These technical rows do not extend linked private-transcript/content lifetime.
8 custody: the original BSD lifecycle source stays canonical under its pending physical family; the proposed operation stores only redacted refs, original identity, semantic commitment and exact first receipt. SP-337 externalizes oversized bodies and every stored value is separately measured at 16 KiB. Storage holds the original first receipt/full-value commitment; coherent backup/restore includes the actual lifecycle source, operation, payload packs, original receipt and controls. Every current read/retry/replay/restore validates original custody and present access/deletion/withdrawal. Raw retained quarantine output and the advisor private transcript are never rendered by the event reader. Deleted bodies stay unavailable; retained metadata is not permission to recreate content.
9 transitions: Records the accepted initial or explicit replacement revision of the frozen BSD workflow/stage binding; opening or cancelling the configuration modal records no event. The actual cmd.bsd.workflow.configure result or accepted workflow start commits the exact policy revision, operational stage bindings and requested/effective identity once. The single start modal does not reopen at every stage. Explicit reconfiguration produces a new immutable binding revision with previous_binding_ref and the owner epoch reset where active assignments are affected; prior reviews retain their original binding. The ten Settings rows expand through BSD-029's exact operational mapping, not a second stage list. An Off stage creates no assignment. Hidden-stage coverage remains advisory and starts no WorkNode or gate. No primary assignment/run/epoch is fabricated for the binding-configuration event.
10 consumers/checkpoints: projector.bsd.workflow_binding_created@1.0.0, reader.bsd.workflow_binding_created@1.0.0 and operating consumer PlanningWorkflow::bsd_stage_binding_projection adopt SP-278 by name via SP-1364. They filter exactly bsd.workflow_binding_created, the actual Project partition and exact supported payload/version. A derived projection references the authentic original event/source state; it does not become canonical assignment/finding/policy state. Checkpoint and all changed projection rows advance atomically by exact prior-value CAS after complete scanned-range proof. Persist only the nine-field durable token; the current read transaction supplies redb_snapshot_id transiently. No GUI-local state, matching-row maximum or caller proof flag supplies currentness.
11 compatibility/withdrawal: There is no earlier admitted BSD event version to migrate or synthesize. The existing completed-review bsd_runtime_record is not this event and never expands into lifecycle history. Genuine future retained 1.0.0 originals remain inspectable under authenticated original admission and recipe after live epoch/config changes, including compatibility-only replay policy; unsupported/missing/substituted custody or withdrawn sources refuse. A writer cutoff first fences new owner operations and drains/resolves previously issued pending inputs, records the exact cutoff under Storage governance, then withdraws the selector. Readers stop on withdrawal, invalidate their publication/checkpoint and rebuild only under an explicitly admitted successor; no fallback aliases, silent migration or fresh effects. Rebuild discards only derived rows, preserves canonical original bytes and reports unavailable expired/lost source rather than claiming empty/success.
12 oracle plan: ATS-1230 and Plans/bsd_event_oracle_plan.json enumerate this exact family's valid paths and one-defect negatives, and scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_events.py executes them (phase 2 and PNC-019 lane s4d, 2026-11-14). Every refusal is one named single-predicate row of a generated Method B guard table of at most eight rows (scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_table_*.py), proved by the gated scripts/pm_guard_isolation.py; a row no input can refuse first sits alone in its own table with a written proof. Every payload field joins its authentic owner source and every payload reference resolves an owner-held object of its kind, subject and Project; the stored logical body joins the same source. Producer crash cuts, lost-acknowledgement retry, no-effect replay, governed withdrawal, successor rebuild, coherent backup restore and the bound retention policy run as behavioural models whose computed outcomes the rows observe. scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_derivation_mutations.py weakens every derivation clause and counts only an accepted witness as a kill; scripts/pm_w3d_bsd_slot_corpus.py runs the shared number and date-time corpus through every integer and timestamp slot; reports/event-authority-20261105/W3D-plan-coverage.json maps each plan entry to its executed rows and witnesses. This is synthetic oracle evidence: writer admission and registry membership were ABSENT during preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration; native execution remains NOT_RUN.
Current membership (2026-11-18) — bsd.workflow_binding_created@1.0.0 is individually registered in Plans/event_family_registry.json. Missing-registration refusal applies only if the exact current family/version/scope registration is absent; this registered family is not refused as missing_event_registration or family_not_admitted merely because it was prepared without admission. Append and checkpoint advance still require every existing schema, scope, retention, original-source, receipt, permission and withdrawal check specified here. Registry membership supplies no native execution proof or additional action authority.

claim_audit.text:
Newly authored owner contract, prepared without admission under deck-2 9.a A.
Newly authored identity for bsd.workflow_binding_created: project_only, family_revision=1.0.0, payload_schema_ref=Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/workflow_binding_created. CV-317/Contracts_V0 section 1.2 owns the complete EventRecord envelope; this unit defines no alternate envelope. project_id equals the original policy/binding Project; assignment-backed payloads join actual primary_run_id to envelope run_id, plus original thread/account/actor/causation values. A configuration-only event has run_id/assignment/epoch/generation null and never invents them. The original trusted operation selects owner_operation_id, from the accepted command_instance_id (manual actions), actual workflow-start dispatch identity (assignment/binding start), actual provider review-result identity (finding/failure/quarantine), or actual owner lifecycle/deadline identity (stop/timeout); a source transition component and the exact subject identity are appended as hex(UTF-8) components to distinguish separate transitions. The canonical operation ID is bsd-op@1:<hex(original_source_id)>:<hex(transition_component)>:<hex(subject_id)>; every component is an exact string from the authentic original source, never a caller assertion or retry clock. This family uses transition_component=bsd.workflow_binding_created and subject_id=binding_id. For multiple decisions about one subject within a review, original_source_id includes that owner decision identity, not merely the review cycle. Recompute from the original source. hex is lowercase byte hex of exact UTF-8, without trimming or normalization. event_id=bsd-event@1:<hex(actual_storage_instance_id)>:<hex(event_type)>:<hex(project_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>; idempotency_key=bsd-key@1:<hex(project_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>. Distinct fields are separated by literal colon and encoded components contain no colon. Use Storage's project~base64url partition and dedupe_by_idempotency_key. The app-root-global ID and lifetime scoped tuple are the envelope owner's identities; application is not admitted here. A future independently authorized application edition must use CV-366 application@1:<hex(server_id)>:<hex(owner_operation_id)>, not this Project recipe. No operation is reminted by retry, restored focus or changed current epoch. SP-1365 defines the pending original-source wrappers; source_state_ref names the exact immutable source wrapper for this operation and its body is validated under the existing logical BSD schema. Binding, assignment, review and finding references resolve those exact owner objects, including their project/run/epoch joins, not merely matching labels. Every other non-constant payload field equals its authentic owner source (the accepted owner decision, the stored logical source body, the immutable review start, the canonical operation or the Project scope), and every payload reference resolves an owner-held object of that field's kind, this subject and this Project before use; the stored logical body's own identity fields join the same authentic source. Producer semantic digest is exactly the envelope-owner RFC8785/SHA-256 projection, excluding Storage-assigned sequence_id/observed_at_utc/persisted_at_utc. This family adopts by name the shared CV-1100/SP-1100 number rules (current_integer, storage_uint64, producer_semantic_digest, qualified_jcs, storage_value_bytes and full_value_commitment), the CV-1101 date-time profiles (event_record for occurred_at_utc and AppendReceipt acknowledged_at_utc, storage_utc_z for observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc, event_record for logical-body timestamps) and SP-1101 sealed-receipt retained-recipe dispatch (RetainedDispatcher); it defines no local number, timestamp or recipe code.
Payload Plans/bsd_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/workflow_binding_created is an individually closed root (additionalProperties=false); all required/null/value/type branches and refs must be validated eagerly. Identifiers preserve exact owner strings, with LF/CR forbidden explicitly; digests have exact lengths. Every source reference is a typed opaque locator and still requires original custody, schema/version, source identity and access validation; a matching string or digest is never source authority. The event stores metadata and redacted refs, never policy instructions, finding claim bodies, advisor transcript or quarantine raw output. Retained record validation uses its authenticated original schema/recipe/admission; it does not pass through these current-write type/format/epoch tests. SP-337 externalizes the referenced source bodies. This EventRecord 2.0.0 family keeps its closed payload inline (payload_ref null): only the EventRecord 3.0.0 successor materializes the SP-337 event-payload reference route and this family has not adopted it, so an inline payload above 16 KiB is refused, never externalized. projector_replay_only is a historical-reader route and is refused by a current append/retry. No family membership or writer selector is added.

The root and both payload editions are closed; application and Project are separate schema IDs, never a nullable rewrite of the old swept schema. CV-366/WorkflowScopeV2 scope joins apply: envelope scope_kind equals payload scope.scope_kind; envelope project_id equals scope.project_id, null only for application, with exact Server and storage instance. Freeze actual Computer/thread/root authority from original input, never focus, Settings, HOME or main fallback. EventRecord event_type is `bundle.selection_forward_blocked`, schema/version dispatch selects the exact edition; occurred_at_utc equals ts, actor_ref equals original actor, body transport under SP-337 below, and thread joins the actual original source/committed record. No synthetic run/node/attempt joins. For bundle.selection_forward_blocked, freeze operation_id from the original accepted operation before its effect (fresh entropy for a new operation, retained across retries). The semantic identity tuple is ["bundle.selection_forward_blocked", "1.0.0", storage_instance_id, scope, computer_id, thread_id, operation_id]; use RFC 8785 canonical JSON UTF-8, event_id = "evt_dch_" + SHA-256(tuple). Project idempotency_key = "dch:" + that same hex digest, with CV-365/Storage exact scope_partition = "project~" + unpadded base64url(UTF-8(project_id)); validate encoding and decoded exact Project identity before append or read. Application explicitly adopts CV-366: idempotency_key = "application@1:" + lowercase hex(UTF-8(scope.server_id)) + ":" + lowercase hex(UTF-8(operation_id)). Here owner_operation_id is exactly this family's original operation_id, frozen with the accepted source before any effect; no retry, timestamp, focus or result component is added. No additional optional effect component is defined for this family; distinct event types retain separate Storage lifetime tuples (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key). Exact original Server/Computer/thread/source joins remain mandatory, including on same-key retries. Same operation and semantic digest returns the original result and first receipt without a new effect; a different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe yields dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Application must never use the Project dch: recipe. Capture original payload and EventRecord semantic digest; same identity with changed semantics is a conflict, never an overwrite. Unknown version or scope is quarantined/unavailable. Earlier shape-only schemas remain unadopted. A payload change requires a new version/edition and governed migration; readers never rewrite original identities or payload bytes.
