claim_audit.text:
catalog.install.completed 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract, prepared without admission before the 2026-11-18 registration. Independent search of current top-level Plans Markdown/JSON and scripts Python found required names at UI_Command_Catalog.md:936 and existing install routing at Wiring_Matrix.md:448, but no exact versioned producer/consumer/checkpoint/identity/withdrawal binding; full per-family negative evidence: /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/drafts/DS15/fix7/catalog_install_completed-search.json. Reuse Section15 §3.13, Commands §6.6/CS-066 and Shared Runtime §4.5. DL-045 authorizes only these missing technical bindings.
Producer: catalog lifecycle controller records the existing subsystem owner effective installation commit. For an executable installation this is verified activation/ready under Shared Runtime §4.5; commands, skills, plugins/hooks, themes and MCP configs use their own canonical install commit. Never substitute download, queue acceptance, a UI acknowledgement or a universal executable machine for that owner outcome. Keep cmd.catalog.install_item as the existing route; item_type is command, skill, plugin, hook, theme or mcp_config. No update/remove admission, active-item/deferred outcome or deletion choice is made. Existing owners resolve item, version, source and actual namespace; an unavailable or ambiguous owner outcome stays unavailable without a fabricated install success.
Scope: actual Project or application namespace as selected by the existing item owner, including actual user/Computer/profile. Project ids are real; application project_id is null, never synthetic. Project partition is Storage project~base64url. Scope key for checkpoint namespace is SHA-256 of canonical MessagePack scope map in UTF-8 key order. Identity: stable original event_id allocated once; Idempotency key is application scope: application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; Project scope: sha256(canonical MessagePack array ["catalog.install.completed", "1.0.0", actual scope map with UTF-8 sorted keys, operation_id]). Application server_id and original_operation_id come from the immutable existing owner operation source, never focus/time. Compare caller-supplied CV-317 semantic body only on retries, excluding Storage-assigned sequence/timestamps; changed semantic bytes conflict with no new effect.
Payload: exact closed Plans/ds15_catalog_install_completed.schema.json; bounded refs only, no executable/config/command bodies, local paths, secrets or installation content. outcome_ref and optional installation_ref resolve the existing owner original transition. Context catalog_owner_payload is the immutable resolved owner outcome, not caller assertion; phase and all fields must match. SP-337 keeps content above 16384 bytes in owner-resolved payload refs, never oversized metadata.
Ordering: adopt SP-286 / CV-339 full-value original outcome, append and first AppendReceipt. Commit existing owner outcome, freeze original event, single writer append/dedupe, retain original receipt/value, then publish. Missing outcome or coherent backup closure is unavailable; no repeat install on retry or replay. Current writes/retries use dedupe_by_idempotency_key and refuse projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable. Retained supported replay-only history remains readable after authenticating original transition, outcome, source and full-value commitment, independently of current live install state. Current permission, owner authorization, deletion/sharing and withdrawal still fence disclosure.
Consumer: reader.ds15.catalog_install_completed.v1@1.0.0, Catalog installation history reader for only catalog.install.completed@1.0.0, adopts SP-278 by name and DL-076 nine-field token. Checkpoint key projector.checkpoint.ds15.catalog_install_completed:{scope_key}, value Plans/ds15_catalog_install_completed_checkpoint.schema.json. Capture CURRENT-selected complete global range and live redb_snapshot_id; persist only nine-field durable token, never the live snapshot. Scan every global row, resolve each matching event original custody and join id/type/scope/partition/Storage sequence. CAS complete previous checkpoint and new checkpoint in one redb transaction; gaps/omissions, changed token/snapshot/source/access or any contradictory original preserve previous. through_sequence_id is globally scanned frontier; last_event_id is last verified matching event. No checkpoint before first match; zero-match suffix retains prior last event. Rebuild requires complete retained prefix and fresh current access.
Compatibility and withdrawal: supported exact 1.0.0 event/reader only; unknown version/field refuses before effects/checkpoint. Withdrawal fences new admissions at committed source frontier, drains only original admitted outcomes/receipts, then fences reader CAS/marks checkpoint withdrawn. Reinstall requires authorization and a complete fresh rebuild; no replay dispatch. Original source/log/receipt backup and redaction/deletion owners remain authoritative. Authority inputs use closed exact-family context schema and exact boolean/bounded integer types before interpretation; malformed values refuse with zero effects.
Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Retention: event and checkpoint retention_policy_ref=PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION; RT must choose between existing receipt/audit or telemetry classes; no policy, expiry or deletion is selected.» At preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, registry membership was absent.
Oracles: ATS-329 and own family fixtures in Plans/ds15_event_contract_fixtures.json, numeric fixtures and scripts/pm-ds15-event-contracts.py cover start/terminal source, false-success queue/admission refusals, semantic retry, full-value custody, Storage joins, replay-only history, permission/deletion, complete coverage/CAS, rebuild and writer/reader withdrawal. Native execution NOT_RUN; static preparation is no production admission.
Round 7 type/source refinement: original_context retains the complete writer transition schema; retained read/checkpoint/rebuild require only current scope and exact-boolean owner authorization, plus the existing disclosure/deletion/share/withdrawal fences. They do not require disposed live transition controls. Plans/ds15_index_inputs.schema.json closes the independent selected global source rows before partition/sequence work. Checkpoint schema/byte validation is the shared checkpoint_value_ok used by actual advance and the static checkpoint_boundary oracle; the boundary grants no advance or append authority.
Round 7 closed evidence carrier: Plans/ds15_original_evidence.schema.json validates original/outcome wrappers, source-map shape and exact carrier metadata types before interpretation; only fields consumed by the operation are required. Original source controls remain frozen, and retained current disclosure context needs only actual subject scope and exact owner authorization. Every envelope joins the complete requested subject scope to the authenticated payload namespace. Candidate semantic body equality is checked before identity/hash construction. Unchanged checkpoint/rebuild results also verify complete selected source and each original Storage join. Pure stored receipt recovery still does not require disposed live transition controls. These are newly authored technical validation bindings, not a native admission.
Current membership (2026-11-18) — catalog.install.completed@1.0.0 is individually registered in Plans/event_family_registry.json. Missing-registration refusal applies only if the exact current family/version/scope registration is absent; this registered family is not refused as missing_event_registration or family_not_admitted merely because it was prepared without admission. Append and checkpoint advance still require every existing schema, scope, retention, original-source, receipt, permission and withdrawal check specified here. Registry membership supplies no native execution proof or additional action authority.

catalog.install.started 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract, prepared without admission before the 2026-11-18 registration. Independent search of current top-level Plans Markdown/JSON and scripts Python found required names at UI_Command_Catalog.md:936 and existing install routing at Wiring_Matrix.md:448, but no exact versioned producer/consumer/checkpoint/identity/withdrawal binding; full per-family negative evidence: /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/drafts/DS15/fix7/catalog_install_started-search.json. Reuse Section15 §3.13, Commands §6.6/CS-066 and Shared Runtime §4.5. DL-045 authorizes only these missing technical bindings.
Producer: catalog lifecycle controller records the existing subsystem owner beginning actual installation work after current consent/policy/source validation, with the immutable owner start outcome committed; dispatch, admission, queued or accepted-only command state is insufficient. Keep cmd.catalog.install_item as the existing route; item_type is command, skill, plugin, hook, theme or mcp_config. No update/remove admission, active-item/deferred outcome or deletion choice is made. Existing owners resolve item, version, source and actual namespace; an unavailable or ambiguous owner outcome stays unavailable without a fabricated install success.
Scope: actual Project or application namespace as selected by the existing item owner, including actual user/Computer/profile. Project ids are real; application project_id is null, never synthetic. Project partition is Storage project~base64url. Scope key for checkpoint namespace is SHA-256 of canonical MessagePack scope map in UTF-8 key order. Identity: stable original event_id allocated once; Idempotency key is application scope: application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; Project scope: sha256(canonical MessagePack array ["catalog.install.started", "1.0.0", actual scope map with UTF-8 sorted keys, operation_id]). Application server_id and original_operation_id come from the immutable existing owner operation source, never focus/time. Compare caller-supplied CV-317 semantic body only on retries, excluding Storage-assigned sequence/timestamps; changed semantic bytes conflict with no new effect.
Payload: exact closed Plans/ds15_catalog_install_started.schema.json; bounded refs only, no executable/config/command bodies, local paths, secrets or installation content. outcome_ref and optional installation_ref resolve the existing owner original transition. Context catalog_owner_payload is the immutable resolved owner outcome, not caller assertion; phase and all fields must match. SP-337 keeps content above 16384 bytes in owner-resolved payload refs, never oversized metadata.
Ordering: adopt SP-286 / CV-339 full-value original outcome, append and first AppendReceipt. Commit existing owner outcome, freeze original event, single writer append/dedupe, retain original receipt/value, then publish. Missing outcome or coherent backup closure is unavailable; no repeat install on retry or replay. Current writes/retries use dedupe_by_idempotency_key and refuse projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable. Retained supported replay-only history remains readable after authenticating original transition, outcome, source and full-value commitment, independently of current live install state. Current permission, owner authorization, deletion/sharing and withdrawal still fence disclosure.

Capture CURRENT-selected complete global range and live redb_snapshot_id; persist only nine-field durable token, never the live snapshot. Scan every global row, resolve each matching event original custody and join id/type/scope/partition/Storage sequence. CAS complete previous checkpoint and new checkpoint in one redb transaction; gaps/omissions, changed token/snapshot/source/access or any contradictory original preserve previous. through_sequence_id is globally scanned frontier; last_event_id is last verified matching event. No checkpoint before first match; zero-match suffix retains prior last event. Rebuild requires complete retained prefix and fresh current access.
Compatibility and withdrawal: supported exact 1.0.0 event/reader only; unknown version/field refuses before effects/checkpoint. Withdrawal fences new admissions at committed source frontier, drains only original admitted outcomes/receipts, then fences reader CAS/marks checkpoint withdrawn. Reinstall requires authorization and a complete fresh rebuild; no replay dispatch. Original source/log/receipt backup and redaction/deletion owners remain authoritative. Authority inputs use closed exact-family context schema and exact boolean/bounded integer types before interpretation; malformed values refuse with zero effects.

Original source controls remain frozen, and retained current disclosure context needs only actual subject scope and exact owner authorization. Every envelope joins the complete requested subject scope to the authenticated payload namespace. Candidate semantic body equality is checked before identity/hash construction. Unchanged checkpoint/rebuild results also verify complete selected source and each original Storage join. Pure stored receipt recovery still does not require disposed live transition controls. These are newly authored technical validation bindings, not a native admission.

Missing-registration refusal applies only if the exact current family/version/scope registration is absent; this registered family is not refused as missing_event_registration or family_not_admitted merely because it was prepared without admission. Closed payload: Plans/ds15_catalog_update_started.schema.json; closed original transition/source schemas: Plans/ds15_deck2_context.schema.json and Plans/ds15_deck2_sources.schema.json, own definitions by exact event name. No raw content, credentials, file paths, executable/configuration bodies, cookies, captures or provider data. All string identifiers/ref fields fully match their schema at the real boundary, including LF refusal. Numbers (sweep 2026-11-08): current inputs follow CV-1100 and SP-1100: raw JSON through loads_current_json, current_integer at every schema integer slot with that slot's own bounds, storage_uint64 for Storage sequence, generation and offset metadata, storage_value_bytes(EVENT_VALUE) for inline-size and identity-preimage bytes, full_value_commitment for CV-339 and the qualified JCS of the CV-317 projection, owner integer paths type-sensitive, before a new append. Retained originals keep the frozen ds15-v1 profile they were written under, selected only through SP-1101 (sweep 2026-11-11): a retained reader or retry resolver first takes one selection from the one write receipt Storage sealed with that exact original (its Storage instance, original ref and CV-339 commitment), never from the Storage instance or family alone, where no custody or no receipt is the existing unavailable contract and more than one receipt or an uninstalled recipe is unsupported, never a fallback to the current or another recipe, and a new append takes the writer's own recipe without reading a receipt; it then resolves the original once through the shared RetainedDispatcher, whose sealed owner authenticates the fetched bytes by their CV-339 commitment and whose frozen verifier recomputes the original, so a coherently rewritten original refuses. Timestamps follow CV-1101 through the shared predicate: every format: date-time takes the EventRecord profile and the Storage-assigned EventRecord observed and persisted times take CV-253's storage_utc_z, for current inputs and retained originals alike; a skipped past format check authorizes no history. No new cap, number codec or date-time grammar is introduced. SP-337 resolves bodies over the 16384-byte inline boundary by original owner payload references; this bounded metadata schema grants no oversized-inline exception. Measure complete encoded envelope payload and checkpoint.
Original source and custody: outcome_ref resolves independently retained owning-component record bytes, never a caller's matching assertion. Reparse and validate the closed exact-family source; join original payload, event_type, scope, Storage instance, original operation identity and original transition observations field by field. The source bank in static fixtures models this owner resolver, not a new production database. Adopt SP-286 / CV-339 full-value original/first-AppendReceipt custody. Commit original transition/source, freeze event, single-writer append/dedupe, retain first receipt and full-value commitment, then publish. Missing original, incoherent closure or unavailable source blocks publication/recovery. Backup/restore preserves original source/log/receipt/consumption closure together. Current authorization, Project/chat permissions, deletion/redaction and sharing withdrawal are rechecked on read; a checkpoint grants no access.
Replay and transitions: retry/lost acknowledgement returns original event_id, immutable outcome and first receipt with zero repeated effects. Recover a missing append with original identity only; never regrant, revoke again, update, remove or issue another notice. Current writer/retry refuses projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable; retained supported 1.0.0 replay-only originals remain readable after authenticating their original transition and source, whatever today's live state. Retained history never requires a disposed current transition control; current disclosure/access/deletion and withdrawal still fence it. Ordinary replay dispatches no command.
Consumer and checkpoint: reader.ds15.catalog_update_started.v1@1.0.0 is the exact operating catalog.update.started history reader and reads only catalog.update.started@1.0.0. Adopt SP-278 and DL-076 nine-field durable read token; key projector.checkpoint.ds15.catalog_update_started:{scope_key}, closed value Plans/ds15_catalog_update_started_checkpoint.schema.json. Physical proposed value: derived redb, coordination_and_storage budget, messagepack_canonical, full encoded value at most 16384 bytes (SP-339/SP-340). This task appends no storage-value registry row and authorizes no physical write/advance. Capture CURRENT-selected complete global range and live snapshot; persist only the nine-field token, never redb_snapshot_id. Scan every global row, resolve each matching original, join event id/type/scope/partition/Storage sequence. Advance by atomic CAS of complete prior and new checkpoint in one redb transaction. Missing rows, contradictions, mismatched token/Storage/snapshot/source, changed access or reader version preserve prior. through_sequence_id is the global scanned frontier and last_event_id the last verified match; no checkpoint before first match, a zero-match suffix keeps the earlier last event. Rebuild requires complete retained prefix and fresh permissions.
Retention: Event and checkpoint adopt DL-401 G11 / RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE@1.0.0: creation anchored, metadata/references only, no age/count expiry or count cap, holds and Storage pressure/fail-closed budget rules remain. Neither retained installation history nor a removal event retains executable, configuration, skill, theme, user override or external-service content forever. Retention premise evidence is DL-401 and G10/G11/G14 as named for this exact family in Plans/storage-plan.md, landed on origin/main; those lines are byte-identical at origin/plans/ea-retention-cards2-20261105 commit 9b76338594c6f1ca75de6c757e7a8b98ab68e229; none of items 4.c-4.f changes that grouping. Referenced content follows its own independently approved lifetime, redaction and read access.
Compatibility and withdrawal: exact 1.0.0 writer/reader/schema only. Unknown version/field fails closed. Writer withdrawal uses committed admission frontier, refuses new admissions and drains only already-admitted original outcomes/receipts; reader withdrawal fences CAS and marks checkpoints withdrawn. Reinstallation needs current authorization and a complete retained-source rebuild. No fabricated old recipe selector; shared number/format historical-selector defects remain explicit sweep work.
Oracles: ATS-329's exact catalog.update.started section, Plans/ds15_deck2_fixtures.json own family row, and python3 scripts/pm-ds15-deck2-contracts.py --family catalog.update.started. Each negative has one declared defect and explicit coherent derived observations; fixture source/custody joins are verified against actual retained values. Native execution NOT_RUN. At preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, registry membership was ABSENT; preparation itself granted no admission, new feature, Decision Log entry or readiness claim.
Current membership (2026-11-18) — catalog.update.started@1.0.0 is individually registered in Plans/event_family_registry.json. Missing-registration refusal applies only if the exact current family/version/scope registration is absent; this registered family is not refused as missing_event_registration or family_not_admitted merely because it was prepared without admission. Append and checkpoint advance still require every existing schema, scope, retention, original-source, receipt, permission and withdrawal check specified here. Registry membership supplies no native execution proof or additional action authority.

A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

claim_audit.text: Newly authored owner contract under DL-090 for collaboration.completed, prepared without admission. It records a run ending completed. Payload CV-466, persistence SP-466, oracles ATS-236; kept as long as the run's chat exists, RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0 materialized.

Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

A refused event appends nothing and changes no row.

claim_audit.text: **Replay, rebuild and withdrawal.** Replay runs in canonical seglog order from the checkpoint's inclusive cursor and only rebuilds projection rows: no message delivery, dispatch, card, notification, command or append follows from replay. Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A refused event appends nothing and changes no row.

claim_audit.text: **Replay, rebuild and withdrawal.** Replay runs in canonical seglog order from the checkpoint's inclusive cursor and only rebuilds projection rows: no message delivery, dispatch, card, notification, command or append follows from replay. Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

claim_audit.text: Newly authored owner contract under DL-090 for collaboration.paused, prepared without admission. It records the run reaching the paused state at a safe boundary after a user's cmd.collaboration.pause. It is emitted when the pause has reached its safe boundary and the owner has committed the run record in state paused, with participant state, the pending inbox, transcript, artifacts and composer-target text preserved. The request alone records nothing; the event is appended when the state is reached. Never for a waiting state (a quota wait, a permission decision, a scheduled window, a Chat Room between rounds with pause_between_rounds on, or a room that used all its rounds), for blocked, for application automation Pause (DL-292: operational state with its own epoch) or for a pause request that has not reached its boundary. DL-091 adds no event for waiting or blocked. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

claim_audit.text: **Admission order.** `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` admits one event at a time under the existing Storage append-writer lock: (1) **exact retry**: the dedupe identity `(scope_partition, event_type, idempotency_key)` with the same producer semantic digest returns the original event and result, its receipt only through `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2`; the same identity with another digest is `idempotency_conflict` and appends nothing; (2) **family admission**: a type the registry does not admit, or an application edition still marked `requires_owner_adoption`, is quarantined before append and advances no checkpoint; (3) **payload**: the edition's CV-460 to CV-478 definition and the EventRecord joins; (4) **current projection**: the projector first brings the checkpoint up to the verified tail of the scope partition under the same lock, or the call returns `collaboration_projection_unavailable` and appends nothing; (5) **transition**: the family's own unit checks the event against the current rows and returns `collaboration_conflict` with one `conflict_kind` on refusal; (6) **append** through the ordinary EventRecord path with SP-336's single data sync for the group, then first-receipt custody. A refused event appends nothing and changes no row.

claim_audit.text: **Replay, rebuild and withdrawal.** Replay runs in canonical seglog order from the checkpoint's inclusive cursor and only rebuilds projection rows: no message delivery, dispatch, card, notification, command or append follows from replay. Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

claim_audit.text: Nine prepared exact families in Plans/debug_investigation_event_fixtures.json have independent closed-payload, identity, Project join, replay/idempotency, original-receipt, custody, compatibility and withdrawal oracles in scripts/pm-debug-investigation-events.py. DL-428 state_changed covers all six Failed reasons and rejects every other failure pairing, separates failed_cleanup, compares original before-state/phase, refuses terminal in-place restart and preserves historical opening/new-linked-work semantics. DL-429 instrumentation_state_changed covers every approved transition row and each source alternative, all eight legal pairs, whole-lane never-needed proof, verified removal including detach, exact visible leftovers/recovery, retry authorization/count/attempt ceiling, pending handoff acceptance, retained responsibility on failure, no second unaccepted handoff, no cleaned restart, restore/permission/overlap guards and immutable original detail joins. Each current writer/retry refuses projector_replay_only; every family has its own missing-field/version/unknown-field, encoded project partition, changed semantic digest, native custody/CAS/permission/withdrawal obligations and none_required transient-checkpoint assertion. The pre-existing seven contracts and mode-resolution cases retain their prior scope. Eagerly resolve every schema reference, including unvisited definitions; malformed references fail the whole checker. Retained original positives ignore current live transition state and current-writer replay policy while forged or withdrawn originals refuse. scripts/pm-debug-investigation-standing-checks.py promotes each family's bad candidates and rejects successful exits masquerading as failure. Static fixtures use projected original facts; they never prove native receipt, proof dereference, payload-pack, writer exclusion, recovery, CAS or effects. Those obligations remain authored and NOT_RUN. Number, physical and date-time checks call the shared helpers of CV-1100, SP-1100 and CV-1101 (current_integer at every companion-schema integer slot with its schema bounds, qualified RFC 8785 identity and producer digests, EVENT_VALUE inline sizes, exact uint64 Storage metadata, date_time with the EventRecord profile and with CV-253 storage_utc_z), and the shared number corpus runs through the complete checker. Every refusal is a named guard-table row proved by the shared guard-isolation tool. No local number, date-time or proof helper is introduced.

claim_audit.text: **Compaction and crash convergence.** Build a complete target shadow under existing compaction intent/journal/lease and exact retained semantic set. DL-428 state_changed covers all six Failed reasons and rejects every other failure pairing, separates failed_cleanup, compares original before-state/phase, refuses terminal in-place restart and preserves historical opening/new-linked-work semantics. DL-429 instrumentation_state_changed covers every approved transition row and each source alternative, all eight legal pairs, whole-lane never-needed proof, verified removal including detach, exact visible leftovers/recovery, retry authorization/count/attempt ceiling, pending handoff acceptance, retained responsibility on failure, no second unaccepted handoff, no cleaned restart, restore/permission/overlap guards and immutable original detail joins. Each current writer/retry refuses projector_replay_only; every family has its own missing-field/version/unknown-field, encoded project partition, changed semantic digest, native custody/CAS/permission/withdrawal obligations and none_required transient-checkpoint assertion. The pre-existing seven contracts and mode-resolution cases retain their prior scope. Eagerly resolve every schema reference, including unvisited definitions; malformed references fail the whole checker. Retained original positives ignore current live transition state and current-writer replay policy while forged or withdrawn originals refuse. scripts/pm-debug-investigation-standing-checks.py promotes each family's bad candidates and rejects successful exits masquerading as failure. Static fixtures use projected original facts; they never prove native receipt, proof dereference, payload-pack, writer exclusion, recovery, CAS or effects. Those obligations remain authored and NOT_RUN. Number, physical and date-time checks call the shared helpers of CV-1100, SP-1100 and CV-1101 (current_integer at every companion-schema integer slot with its schema bounds, qualified RFC 8785 identity and producer digests, EVENT_VALUE inline sizes, exact uint64 Storage metadata, date_time with the EventRecord profile and with CV-253 storage_utc_z), and the shared number corpus runs through the complete checker. Every refusal is a named guard-table row proved by the shared guard-isolation tool. No local number, date-time or proof helper is introduced.

claim_audit.text: Custody: Storage owns the immutable EventRecord and first receipt under coherent seglog/index/receipt backup and verified restore. Runtime Artifacts keeps original evidence/manifests under its own policies and source identity; the investigation owner keeps binding/item/instrumentation originals. Check scope, current read permission, deletion/tombstone and revocation at each dereference and export; missing or inaccessible refs yield unavailable/omitted evidence, never raw fallback. Bounded summary strings are scrubbed before persistence and preserve omission/redaction state in their original referenced owner record; no raw logs, binary bytes, credentials, cookies or secrets may enter the payload. This contract changes no evidence deletion right or lifetime. No choice, TTL, count eviction or orphan-thread rule is authorized here. It owns no additional stored value; the pre-existing deferred debug_investigation_record.v1 inventory is not materialized by these transient readers.

Ordering is by canonical source order, not timestamps. A complete survivor index can be fresh relative to verified survivors while `health=degraded`; loss provenance and global integrity/mutation fences remain. A reader pinned to an older coherent snapshot may finish only under the existing fence/lease; it cannot claim the latest boundary or disclose after invalidation.

claim_audit.text: **Compaction and crash convergence.** Build a complete target shadow under existing compaction intent/journal/lease and exact retained semantic set. The staged checkpoint is durably registered but never current. The old current node continues to win while CURRENT is proven unchanged. All target rows and staged frontier must be complete and mutually consistent before the existing synchronized CURRENT promotion. After CURRENT selects target, old index rows immediately cease to be current authority; startup activates the verified complete target shadow or rebuilds from target survivors. In a single redb transaction, activate the target, update `current_generation_id`, retire the old node with its first retirement time and successor, and clear the existing pending-generation state. No checkpoint can roll CURRENT back or choose a source by mtime. Ambiguous controls follow Case L's existing recovery-required fence.

WorkflowScopeV2, logical pm.workflow_scope.v2 version 2.0.0, is the single explicit application/Project scope contract at Plans/shared_integration_runtime.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowScopeV2. Its required members are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, scope_partition, server_id, project_id, project_home_server_id and named_plan_id; no unknown members. server_id is the real owning Server, not a display Computer or client device. Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. A scope is not an execution context: Server-owned Settings/pause need no fabricated thread; every chat/task execution envelope additionally requires actual thread/Server/Host/Environment/root identities and applicable run/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule refs. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.

Conversion reissues destination auth/route/permission rather than reusing source capability. Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. Explicit projects.* reads owned by Plans/Tools.md and Plans/Permissions_System.md use current source-Computer access and coverage; actual Project writes use that Project’s chat/owner/conversion.

claim_audit.text:
The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. A schema/source row is not an append or event-checkpoint grant. settings.layer.changed is application-only; normal chat/history/run/tool/Usage/recovery/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule/attention/layout app variants are application_or_project only for their actual admitted writer. Every selected variant must join full original source, commit/append/first-receipt, canonical or derived read/checkpoint, backup/restore and retention. New approval.chat_tool_requested/resolved payloads are thread/tool/target bound, distinct from Project Orchestrator node approval events. Wizard handoff, PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/WorkNode/gates and frozen Workflow/certified sources stay Project-only. Unknown/missing source, version or family is unavailable/quarantined; a registry or all-true fixture boolean cannot admit native writes. Existing notebook/plugin/auth/pause/scheduler candidate/non-emitting dispositions remain until their own complete admission. goal.paused/resumed or any other required unregistered semantic name cannot emit by inference; missing_event_registration is preserved. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.
CV-740 explicitly selects the separate header-bearing app board V2 whole source/message/wrapper graph
for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.
CV-1100 and SP-1101 govern exact input and authenticated original-recipe dispatch; this unit retains its typed semantic tree, app float64/binary physical profile, closed kinds, exact prefixes and original Project codecs.

Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.

claim_audit.text: **Recovery and withdrawal authority for `filesafe.destructive_override_denied` (review round 1).** The durable original-operation journal starts pending at owner commit, before preparation, and remains pending until its original receipt and dependent terminal publication are reconciled. Crash discards volatile prepared/event/receipt caches; recovery restores them only from the durable phase and authoritative issued full value plus unchanged first receipt. Recovery refusal persists and fences terminal/outbox publication and every cached retry until explicit successful same-operation recovery. Each subsequent terminal/retry resolves complete SP-286 custody again; presence of an event key or an old memory receipt is insufficient. After issuance, retained duplicate resolution uses issued EventRecord/receipt custody independently of disposed original command, approval or mutation controls, and performs no domain reexecution. A body-dependent read can still be unavailable under its own owner policy.

WorkflowScopeV2, logical pm.workflow_scope.v2 version 2.0.0, is the single explicit application/Project scope contract at Plans/shared_integration_runtime.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowScopeV2. Its required members are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, scope_partition, server_id, project_id, project_home_server_id and named_plan_id; no unknown members. server_id is the real owning Server, not a display Computer or client device. Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. A scope is not an execution context: Server-owned Settings/pause need no fabricated thread; every chat/task execution envelope additionally requires actual thread/Server/Host/Environment/root identities and applicable run/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule refs. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.
CV-169’s reconciled route vocabulary includes application. App routes, WebSocket identity, permission and payload contexts bind exact scope/object/Server and issued currentness/return. Conversion reissues destination auth/route/permission rather than reusing source capability. Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. Explicit projects.* reads owned by Plans/Tools.md and Plans/Permissions_System.md use current source-Computer access and coverage; actual Project writes use that Project’s chat/owner/conversion.
Thread preview is a typed local draft projection: ui.thread.request.preview and ui.thread.spawn.preview, not new domain commands or fresh authority. Send reuses the registered cmd.thread.request -> handlers::thread::request and cmd.thread.spawn -> handlers::thread::spawn; cmd.thread.await retains its existing wait owner and adds the explicitly selected ThreadAwaitRequestScopeV2/ThreadAwaitResultScopeV2 compatibility union. The proposed cmd.thread.request.preview/send and cmd.thread.spawn.preview/send spellings are rejected duplicates, not aliases. New ThreadRequestFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 and ThreadSpawnFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 live at Plans/application_workflow_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/<name>, each logical pm.thread.<request|spawn>.facade_<request|result>.v2 version 2.0.0. Legacy requests retain their exact interpretation; the new send variants are explicit schema/version selectors and do not add operation=preview.
A preview binds sender scope/thread/Computer/mode and receiver scope/thread or bounded requested child role, exact bounded body/context ref+hash, parent Goal/Plan/run/agent lineage, request/spawn id, permission ceiling, target/topology/body generations, automatic_round_trip_count, offline expiry and origin return. Keep protected input/credential bytes out. preview_sha256 uses CV-366’s thread-preview domain; expires_at and the captured revisions make stale state explicit. Result display is truthful draft/as-of state, not an allow receipt. Send revalidates actual source/target/mode/Off/permission/Stop/body/preview/currentness immediately before the one durable outbox commit. Request uses request_id, spawn uses spawn_request_id; conflicting same identity/digest refuses, duplicate same intent returns the original continuity result. No new conversation transport, branch command or queue is created. Incoming receiver-owned accept/decline uses the existing commands owned by Plans/Commands_System.md; sender authority never changes receiver mode or answers its retained approvals. Three automatic round trips and one-day offline expiry remain. Return preserves exact request/child/target/initiating Client, route/focus/context revision and continuation generation. Preview is no-persist/no EventRecord; Send keeps existing continuity/outbox result and no EventRecord pending Event Authority. Handler absence remains handler_unavailable. The local preview envelope defs ThreadFacadePreviewLocalActionRequestV2 and ThreadFacadePreviewLocalActionResultV2 also live in the new app resource; logical IDs are pm.thread.facade_preview.local_request.v2 and pm.thread.facade_preview.local_result.v2, both 2.0.0. No facade or ScopeV2 alias is added inside full_thread_runtime_contracts.schema.json or goal_runtime_contracts.schema.json or goal_body_custody.schema.json: their whole bytes are selected by ten frozen source manifests. General aggregate companions not selected whole by a frozen bank may add $ref aliases while retaining original definitions; any selected-whole aggregate uses a new-resource alias instead. Pure conversation/internal planning carries an explicit empty admitted-root set and null working_directory until an actual file/command creates the lazy folder or a directory grant supplies a root. Null cwd never launches a process or triggers HOME/CWD/Project fallback.
Application-only logical codecs constrain WorkflowScopeV2 to scope_kind=application, including schedule, quota consent, artifact, Home and Goal payload siblings. A physical wrapper joins its complete scope, server_id and storage_instance_id to the corresponding logical fields or application_context; individually valid but different outer/inner identities refuse before custody or dispatch. Project codecs remain separate.
ThreadAwaitRequestApplicationV2 binds actual app sender context, original request_id/await_request_id, exact receiver scope/thread/generation, condition, expiry, outbox evidence and reply route without Project Home Server or Source Location placeholders. Its result preserves those joins and the existing ordered reply sequence, expiry, cancellation and idempotent wait identity. ThreadAwaitRequestScopeV2/ResultScopeV2 preserve the historical Project request/result exactly and use handlers::thread::await_condition for both app-to-Project and app-to-app waits; a reply from another request, receiver or sequence cannot settle this wait.
SettingsOperationContextV1 carries actual record scope/storage, actor, permission/writer generations, initiating Client route/focus and idempotent return. Its settings_surface/setup origin has no execution root or task/thread requirement; a thread origin embeds the unchanged strict WorkflowCommandContextV1. Selected Settings preview/apply/rollback V3 compatibility unions add this owner context, with exact destination level/Computer/Device and preview generation joins. AttachmentOwnerContextV1 instead discriminates pre-message draft ownership from committed-thread execution, preserving actual Host/root and composer identity. StarterCatalogContextV1 is an application record/catalog owner context without a thread. These editions do not weaken execution contexts or mint a thread/Project for owner metadata work.

WorkflowScopeV2, logical pm.workflow_scope.v2 version 2.0.0, is the single explicit application/Project scope contract at Plans/shared_integration_runtime.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowScopeV2. Its required members are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, scope_partition, server_id, project_id, project_home_server_id and named_plan_id; no unknown members. server_id is the real owning Server, not a display Computer or client device. Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. A scope is not an execution context: Server-owned Settings/pause need no fabricated thread; every chat/task execution envelope additionally requires actual thread/Server/Host/Environment/root identities and applicable run/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule refs. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.

Conversion reissues destination auth/route/permission rather than reusing source capability. Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. Explicit projects.* reads owned by Plans/Tools.md and Plans/Permissions_System.md use current source-Computer access and coverage; actual Project writes use that Project’s chat/owner/conversion.

claim_audit.text:
The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. A schema/source row is not an append or event-checkpoint grant. settings.layer.changed is application-only; normal chat/history/run/tool/Usage/recovery/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule/attention/layout app variants are application_or_project only for their actual admitted writer. Every selected variant must join full original source, commit/append/first-receipt, canonical or derived read/checkpoint, backup/restore and retention. New approval.chat_tool_requested/resolved payloads are thread/tool/target bound, distinct from Project Orchestrator node approval events. Wizard handoff, PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/WorkNode/gates and frozen Workflow/certified sources stay Project-only. Unknown/missing source, version or family is unavailable/quarantined; a registry or all-true fixture boolean cannot admit native writes. Existing notebook/plugin/auth/pause/scheduler candidate/non-emitting dispositions remain until their own complete admission. goal.paused/resumed or any other required unregistered semantic name cannot emit by inference; missing_event_registration is preserved. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.
CV-740 explicitly selects the separate header-bearing app board V2 whole source/message/wrapper graph
for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.
CV-1100 and SP-1101 govern exact input and authenticated original-recipe dispatch; this unit retains its typed semantic tree, app float64/binary physical profile, closed kinds, exact prefixes and original Project codecs.

WorkflowScopeV2, logical pm.workflow_scope.v2 version 2.0.0, is the single explicit application/Project scope contract at Plans/shared_integration_runtime.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowScopeV2. Its required members are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, scope_partition, server_id, project_id, project_home_server_id and named_plan_id; no unknown members. server_id is the real owning Server, not a display Computer or client device. Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. A scope is not an execution context: Server-owned Settings/pause need no fabricated thread; every chat/task execution envelope additionally requires actual thread/Server/Host/Environment/root identities and applicable run/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule refs. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.
CV-169’s reconciled route vocabulary includes application. App routes, WebSocket identity, permission and payload contexts bind exact scope/object/Server and issued currentness/return. Conversion reissues destination auth/route/permission rather than reusing source capability. Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. Explicit projects.* reads owned by Plans/Tools.md and Plans/Permissions_System.md use current source-Computer access and coverage; actual Project writes use that Project’s chat/owner/conversion.
Thread preview is a typed local draft projection: ui.thread.request.preview and ui.thread.spawn.preview, not new domain commands or fresh authority. Send reuses the registered cmd.thread.request -> handlers::thread::request and cmd.thread.spawn -> handlers::thread::spawn; cmd.thread.await retains its existing wait owner and adds the explicitly selected ThreadAwaitRequestScopeV2/ThreadAwaitResultScopeV2 compatibility union. The proposed cmd.thread.request.preview/send and cmd.thread.spawn.preview/send spellings are rejected duplicates, not aliases. New ThreadRequestFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 and ThreadSpawnFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 live at Plans/application_workflow_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/<name>, each logical pm.thread.<request|spawn>.facade_<request|result>.v2 version 2.0.0. Legacy requests retain their exact interpretation; the new send variants are explicit schema/version selectors and do not add operation=preview.
A preview binds sender scope/thread/Computer/mode and receiver scope/thread or bounded requested child role, exact bounded body/context ref+hash, parent Goal/Plan/run/agent lineage, request/spawn id, permission ceiling, target/topology/body generations, automatic_round_trip_count, offline expiry and origin return. Keep protected input/credential bytes out. preview_sha256 uses CV-366’s thread-preview domain; expires_at and the captured revisions make stale state explicit. Result display is truthful draft/as-of state, not an allow receipt. Send revalidates actual source/target/mode/Off/permission/Stop/body/preview/currentness immediately before the one durable outbox commit. Request uses request_id, spawn uses spawn_request_id; conflicting same identity/digest refuses, duplicate same intent returns the original continuity result. The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.

for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.

claim_audit.text: **Recovery and withdrawal authority for `filesafe.guard_init_failed` (review round 1).** The durable original-operation journal starts pending at owner commit, before preparation, and remains pending until its original receipt and dependent terminal publication are reconciled. Crash discards volatile prepared/event/receipt caches; recovery restores them only from the durable phase and authoritative issued full value plus unchanged first receipt. Recovery refusal persists and fences terminal/outbox publication and every cached retry until explicit successful same-operation recovery. Each subsequent terminal/retry resolves complete SP-286 custody again; presence of an event key or an old memory receipt is insufficient. After issuance, retained duplicate resolution uses issued EventRecord/receipt custody independently of disposed original command, approval or mutation controls, and performs no domain reexecution. A body-dependent read can still be unavailable under its own owner policy.
