WorkflowScopeV2, logical pm.workflow_scope.v2 version 2.0.0, is the single explicit application/Project scope contract at Plans/shared_integration_runtime.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowScopeV2. Its required members are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, scope_partition, server_id, project_id, project_home_server_id and named_plan_id; no unknown members. server_id is the real owning Server, not a display Computer or client device. Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. A scope is not an execution context: Server-owned Settings/pause need no fabricated thread; every chat/task execution envelope additionally requires actual thread/Server/Host/Environment/root identities and applicable run/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule refs. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.
CV-169’s reconciled route vocabulary includes application. App routes, WebSocket identity, permission and payload contexts bind exact scope/object/Server and issued currentness/return. Conversion reissues destination auth/route/permission rather than reusing source capability. Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. Explicit projects.* reads owned by Plans/Tools.md and Plans/Permissions_System.md use current source-Computer access and coverage; actual Project writes use that Project’s chat/owner/conversion.
Thread preview is a typed local draft projection: ui.thread.request.preview and ui.thread.spawn.preview, not new domain commands or fresh authority. Send reuses the registered cmd.thread.request -> handlers::thread::request and cmd.thread.spawn -> handlers::thread::spawn; cmd.thread.await retains its existing wait owner and adds the explicitly selected ThreadAwaitRequestScopeV2/ThreadAwaitResultScopeV2 compatibility union. The proposed cmd.thread.request.preview/send and cmd.thread.spawn.preview/send spellings are rejected duplicates, not aliases. New ThreadRequestFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 and ThreadSpawnFacadeRequestV2/ResultV2 live at Plans/application_workflow_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/<name>, each logical pm.thread.<request|spawn>.facade_<request|result>.v2 version 2.0.0. Legacy requests retain their exact interpretation; the new send variants are explicit schema/version selectors and do not add operation=preview.
A preview binds sender scope/thread/Computer/mode and receiver scope/thread or bounded requested child role, exact bounded body/context ref+hash, parent Goal/Plan/run/agent lineage, request/spawn id, permission ceiling, target/topology/body generations, automatic_round_trip_count, offline expiry and origin return. Keep protected input/credential bytes out. preview_sha256 uses CV-366’s thread-preview domain; expires_at and the captured revisions make stale state explicit. Result display is truthful draft/as-of state, not an allow receipt. Send revalidates actual source/target/mode/Off/permission/Stop/body/preview/currentness immediately before the one durable outbox commit. Request uses request_id, spawn uses spawn_request_id; conflicting same identity/digest refuses, duplicate same intent returns the original continuity result. No new conversation transport, branch command or queue is created. Incoming receiver-owned accept/decline uses the existing commands owned by Plans/Commands_System.md; sender authority never changes receiver mode or answers its retained approvals. Three automatic round trips and one-day offline expiry remain. Return preserves exact request/child/target/initiating Client, route/focus/context revision and continuation generation. Preview is no-persist/no EventRecord; Send keeps existing continuity/outbox result and no EventRecord pending Event Authority. Handler absence remains handler_unavailable. The local preview envelope defs ThreadFacadePreviewLocalActionRequestV2 and ThreadFacadePreviewLocalActionResultV2 also live in the new app resource; logical IDs are pm.thread.facade_preview.local_request.v2 and pm.thread.facade_preview.local_result.v2, both 2.0.0. No facade or ScopeV2 alias is added inside full_thread_runtime_contracts.schema.json or goal_runtime_contracts.schema.json or goal_body_custody.schema.json: their whole bytes are selected by ten frozen source manifests. General aggregate companions not selected whole by a frozen bank may add $ref aliases while retaining original definitions; any selected-whole aggregate uses a new-resource alias instead. Pure conversation/internal planning carries an explicit empty admitted-root set and null working_directory until an actual file/command creates the lazy folder or a directory grant supplies a root. Null cwd never launches a process or triggers HOME/CWD/Project fallback.
Application-only logical codecs constrain WorkflowScopeV2 to scope_kind=application, including schedule, quota consent, artifact, Home and Goal payload siblings. A physical wrapper joins its complete scope, server_id and storage_instance_id to the corresponding logical fields or application_context; individually valid but different outer/inner identities refuse before custody or dispatch. Project codecs remain separate.
ThreadAwaitRequestApplicationV2 binds actual app sender context, original request_id/await_request_id, exact receiver scope/thread/generation, condition, expiry, outbox evidence and reply route without Project Home Server or Source Location placeholders. Its result preserves those joins and the existing ordered reply sequence, expiry, cancellation and idempotent wait identity. ThreadAwaitRequestScopeV2/ResultScopeV2 preserve the historical Project request/result exactly and use handlers::thread::await_condition for both app-to-Project and app-to-app waits; a reply from another request, receiver or sequence cannot settle this wait.
SettingsOperationContextV1 carries actual record scope/storage, actor, permission/writer generations, initiating Client route/focus and idempotent return. Its settings_surface/setup origin has no execution root or task/thread requirement; a thread origin embeds the unchanged strict WorkflowCommandContextV1. Selected Settings preview/apply/rollback V3 compatibility unions add this owner context, with exact destination level/Computer/Device and preview generation joins. AttachmentOwnerContextV1 instead discriminates pre-message draft ownership from committed-thread execution, preserving actual Host/root and composer identity. StarterCatalogContextV1 is an application record/catalog owner context without a thread. These editions do not weaken execution contexts or mint a thread/Project for owner metadata work.

claim_audit.text:
The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. A schema/source row is not an append or event-checkpoint grant. settings.layer.changed is application-only; normal chat/history/run/tool/Usage/recovery/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule/attention/layout app variants are application_or_project only for their actual admitted writer. Every selected variant must join full original source, commit/append/first-receipt, canonical or derived read/checkpoint, backup/restore and retention. New approval.chat_tool_requested/resolved payloads are thread/tool/target bound, distinct from Project Orchestrator node approval events. Wizard handoff, PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/WorkNode/gates and frozen Workflow/certified sources stay Project-only. Unknown/missing source, version or family is unavailable/quarantined; a registry or all-true fixture boolean cannot admit native writes. Existing notebook/plugin/auth/pause/scheduler candidate/non-emitting dispositions remain until their own complete admission. goal.paused/resumed or any other required unregistered semantic name cannot emit by inference; missing_event_registration is preserved. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.
CV-740 explicitly selects the separate header-bearing app board V2 whole source/message/wrapper graph
for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.
CV-1100 and SP-1101 govern exact input and authenticated original-recipe dispatch; this unit retains its typed semantic tree, app float64/binary physical profile, closed kinds, exact prefixes and original Project codecs.

claim_audit.text: Legal sequence gaps are exactly `allocator_lease_abandoned | corruption_loss | retention_compaction` and require actual manifest/owner evidence. Ordering is by canonical source order, not timestamps. A complete survivor index can be fresh relative to verified survivors while `health=degraded`; loss provenance and global integrity/mutation fences remain. An unsupported otherwise-valid future source version stops indexing before that record and prevents a claim of complete current coverage; it is not skipped or quarantined as corruption. Source controls changing during the read invalidate the current token. A reader pinned to an older coherent snapshot may finish only under the existing fence/lease; it cannot claim the latest boundary or disclose after invalidation.

claim_audit.text: **Compaction and crash convergence.** Build a complete target shadow under existing compaction intent/journal/lease and exact retained semantic set. The staged checkpoint is durably registered but never current. The old current node continues to win while CURRENT is proven unchanged. All target rows and staged frontier must be complete and mutually consistent before the existing synchronized CURRENT promotion. After CURRENT selects target, old index rows immediately cease to be current authority; startup activates the verified complete target shadow or rebuilds from target survivors. In a single redb transaction, activate the target, update `current_generation_id`, retire the old node with its first retirement time and successor, and clear the existing pending-generation state. No checkpoint can roll CURRENT back or choose a source by mtime. Ambiguous controls follow Case L's existing recovery-required fence.

Its idempotency_key is 'dt:' plus lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JSON [event_type, scope_partition, gate_id, run_id, evaluation_id], preserving those exact source values. event_id is 'evt_dt_' plus SHA-256 of UTF-8 idempotency_key. Use dedupe_by_idempotency_key and the complete CV-EventRecord producer_semantic_digest; same identity/different semantic digest refuses idempotency_conflict. Retries retain occurred_at_utc and every source/envelope field. The operating consumer storage.dt.gate_evaluation_started.reader.v1@1.0.0 serves progression scheduler, validation reports and inspection; it directly filters verified EventRecord index reads for this exact family, not an invented second domain database. It explicitly adopts SP-278 and DL-076's nine-field durable token, never persisted redb_snapshot_id. The inclusive examined_through_sequence_id advances over every examined source row, including nonmatching rows; last_applied_event_id is the last matching row or null. Validate storage instance, partition, token generation/frontier/coverage/source selection and exact admitted family/version before publication. Process a prefix and publish the cursor/token/filter completeness atomically under exact previous-value CAS and a fenced writer lease; losing CAS publishes nothing. Empty source is proven by the source token, never guessed from no matches. Readers require current/healthy/filter_complete coverage for their requested prefix and recheck current permission, tombstones, source selection and withdrawal before returning any record. Rebuild from verified retained source with recovery holds, never from checkpoint alone; source gaps return unavailable, never silently skip them. Derived checkpoint retention is RP-PROJECTION-3GEN with source holds and at most three same-key generations. Canonical seglog originals and referenced bodies remain under mandatory coherent backup/restore, source access and deletion checks; opaque refs grant no access. Keep credentials, tool arguments, raw output and private file contents out of this payload; refs are opaque permission-checked locators, bounded reasons/previews are redacted before persistence. Backup restores original source, dedupe/receipt custody and references coherently or fences mutation; checkpoints rebuild, and an older restore never revives a resolved approval or deleted worktree. Unknown version refuses current mutation and disclosure until a validating reader/upgrader is installed; legacy aliases normalize before persistence only with original source proof, never by replay side effects. Withdrawal first cuts off this family's append admission, then fences its consumer/readers and marks checkpoint withdrawn with a fixed timestamp. No advance or ordinary read follows; governed compatible rebuild and revalidated source/admission are required to resume. No zero-cursor reset, sibling substitution or history rewrite. retention_policy_ref = RP-RUNTIME-365D. Case L-3 directly names Runtime/run/node/attempt: 365 days after actual run completion, 1,000,000/run and 5,000,000/project, successor compaction. Holds, original anchors and dependency checks are unchanged; retries never reset the retention anchor. Checks and positive/negative fixtures: python3 scripts/pm-dt-event-contracts.py; ATS-292. For gate.evaluation_started alone, the newly authored original-source custody is dt_gate_evaluation_started_source at storage/event-sources/dt/gate_evaluation_started/{event_id}/{stage}.json, strict Plans/dt_event_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/gate_evaluation_started_source; no sibling source is accepted. The codec is pm.dt.source.json.v1 canonical UTF-8 JSON without BOM/newline, maximum 1048576 bytes per stage; reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, malformed Unicode, unknown fields and unsupported version. SHA-256 binds exact bytes; file paths are derived from the validated event_id and literal stage under this Storage instance, never caller paths. ProgressionGateRunner.evaluation_started owns preparation and authenticates ProgressionGateRunner.evaluation_started.resolve_original against the actual original Progression_Gates.md owner_ref/revision, not the caller's witness or today's reconstructed configuration. Install the exact source schema/codec and append admission via StorageMigrationCoordinator, then validate current family admission, scope, actor and all family predicates before preparing or performing work. Publish prepared.json once under the subject owner lock using SP-131 same-directory temp/fsync/no-overwrite promotion and synchronized parent entries; allocate the original identity first. A byte-identical existing stage is reused; different bytes fence the subject. The owner's existing operation commits its result with this source identity in its original outcome; the resolver proves that join against the actual owner transaction/receipt before completed.json is durably promoted. This is a recoverable prepare/outcome handshake, not an atomic commit across an external tool or Git and Storage. A crash after prepare but before provable outcome remains fenced; query the original owner operation by this exact allocated identity. If it cannot prove original outcome, return unavailable and do not repeat any effect. completed.json is immutable, links prepared_sha256, carries the exact redacted closed payload and frozen envelope_context, and names the immutable owner_outcome_ref. Only then append the exact EventRecord; SP-286/CV-339 full-value v2 resolves the first eleven-field receipt, including its original seal-time timestamp. Source and completed payload/identity/envelope joins and current owner permissions/deletion are revalidated under the final owner lock after every helper. For this family require a barrier-class full flush through original outcome/source files, packs, segment commit frame and canonical receipt before terminal publication or authorizing dependent work. This is a stronger event-specific barrier within SP-336/SP-347, not a change to ordinary receipt loss. Lost acknowledgement returns the original full value and receipt; no fabricated replacement time/result/identity. Source stages, original owner outcomes, referenced bodies and full-value receipt custody form one mandatory coherent backup closure. claim_audit.text:
git.clone.completed closed payload
git.clone.completed 1.0.0 — newly authored owner contract under DL-045.
Prepared without admission. Exact payload is Plans/event_payloads/git_clone_completed.schema.json (pm.event_payload.git_clone_completed.v1); no sibling or legacy spelling is admitted. Scope is project_only; project_id is a real immutable Project ID; application scope, null, empty and sentinel Project identities are forbidden. Payload project_id equals the envelope join. Existing CV-365 scope rules remain mandatory. Optional envelope lineage comes from the original operation, never ambient focus. Schema-only validity is insufficient.
Producer: ordinary Git clone terminal adapter. Observe succeeded cmd.source_control.repository.clone with scm_backend=git only after owner native completion, destination verification and terminal operation receipt. The reserved Project/repository/workspace/Host/Environment lineage is original intent data, never focused Project. This precedes Project registration and cannot certify its success. Jujutsu cmd.jujutsu.git.clone is distinct and never normalized to this spelling. Failed, cancelled, effect_unknown or merely accepted ObservableWork emits no completion. Current Source_Control_System sections 7/9 route the old catalog spelling to this ordinary Git producer without reviving cmd.git.clone.
Freeze operation_id from fresh entropy in the original owning operation before its effect; preserve it and all source facts on retry/restart. Freeze the completion payload after owner success, before append. If the original operation cannot durably retain its intent/result, publication fails closed: never rerun the effect to reconstruct evidence. This contract creates no independent operation journal or stored value. The owner retains its existing intent/result and source refs under its existing storage contract.
Adopt SP-286 first-AppendReceipt custody and CV-339 full-value v2 successor by name, including SP-336/SP-347 current group-commit rules. Validate admission before append; absent membership, unresolved retention or unavailable source custody prevents activation. Referenced bodies commit under SP-337 before append. The first original AppendReceipt is exposed only after the durable group frame; terminal event success publication follows that receipt. Lost acknowledgement returns that original full stored result and receipt, never a second effect or new receipt; equal identity with different semantic digest is a conflict, not a retry.
Identity digest is SHA-256 of UTF-8 compact JSON array ["git.clone.completed", "1.0.0", storage_instance_id, payload.project_id, payload.operation_id], with ensure_ascii=false, no whitespace and array order preserved. event_id="evt_"+digest; idempotency_key="git.clone.completed:"+digest; family_revision=1.0.0, replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key, redaction_profile=secret_refs_only. Use Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord for the closed envelope, not a local field list. Envelope occurred_at_utc equals payload.completed_at_utc byte-for-byte from the original ordinary Git clone command operation; retry time is forbidden. Storage alone assigns sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc. Full producer semantic digest uses EventRecord and CV-339, not only the identity tuple.
Exact envelope joins for git.clone.completed: actor_ref is the non-empty non-secret actor reference retained by the original ordinary Git clone command operation from its accepted owner request, never the retrying Client. correlation_id is the non-empty correlation_id frozen by that same original owner operation; payload.operation_id equals its immutable operation_id. Never synthesize either required value as null. Scope/project and the entire frozen payload must equal that original operation result. The original terminal result must join payload.repo_id, workspace_id, host_id, environment_id, source_location_ref and operation_receipt_ref exactly, including the reserved Project identity. Other nullable EventRecord lineage, account, causal and upstream-sequence joins copy the retained original operation facts, including required-present nulls only when that original has no such join; they are never populated from ambient focus. payload_ref is null for this bounded inline payload; enforce Storage's 16 KiB inline canonical MessagePack byte limit before append; new-native migration fields are null. Freeze all these producer values before append and resolve the complete original EventRecord through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1 on receipt-dependent recovery. Required non-null fields retain their schema-required types.
Operating consumer reader.scm.git_clone_completed@1.0.0 uses reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 and projector.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0, explicitly adopting SP-278. It reads this exact event_type/revision/scope only after the complete CURRENT-selected global frontier is verified. Its checkpoint is the existing checkpoints key event_record_index_checkpoint.v1:{storage_instance_id}, value Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint; no family-specific persisted cursor or projection is introduced. Generic rows and frontier advance atomically by the existing SP-278 CAS; a failed CAS preserves the old publication and is retried from a fresh snapshot. Operating reads are passive with no durable progress, so their own checkpoint is explicitly none. Each read uses the exact live ten-field read_token in one real redb snapshot; any stored read token must instead be the nine-field DL-076 durable token with redb_snapshot_id removed, never a persisted snapshot identity. Rebuild uses original retained seglog through SP-278, preserving identity and no side effects. Unauthorized, deleted, unsupported, stale or unresolved source reads return unavailable; they cannot produce empty-success evidence.
Profile rationale for git.clone.completed: source location and original terminal receipt remain behind authorized refs; URLs with credentials and private absolute destinations are forbidden; redaction_profile=secret_refs_only is an existing EventRecord value and does not grant source access.

Identity recipe for this family: use strict UTF-8 canonical JSON of the array ["pm.memory.maintenance.event.v1",storage_instance_id,project_id,operation_id,"memory.index.semantic.rebuild.started"] with no whitespace, ensure_ascii=false; SHA-256 lower hex. event_id="evt_mem_"+digest and idempotency_key="memory-maintenance:"+digest. All ids are nonempty bounded opaque owner-generated identifiers, not user content. The actual native acceptance generates operation_id once, persists it before publication and retries reuse it. request_sha256 binds the exact accepted command arguments and scope; a changed request under the same operation fails idempotency_conflict. Envelope type, payload type, project, correlation and causation must join CV-655.
Original operation custody is the newly authored memory_index_semantic_rebuild_operation family, closed schema Plans/memory_maintenance_operation.schema.json#/$defs/index_semantic_rebuild, key memory_index_semantic_rebuild_operation.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{hex(project_id)}:{hex(operation_id)} in canonical redb table memory_maintenance_operations. Hex is lowercase UTF-8 bytes, reversible and separator-safe. Admit its schema through the actual StorageMigrationCoordinator before any write, never inferred store versions. No duplicate command journal or gist store is created. Initial accepted row and request digest commit before append. This family explicitly adopts SP-286 and CV-339 full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody: validate admission, append barrier-class SeglogFrameV2 through SP-026/SP-236 with full flush, durably settle original receipt, then advance operation state. New issuance uses v2; resolve_full_value.v1 verifies the exact original event; missing/legacy-only proof fences dependent state. Lost delivery resolves the original receipt and cannot mint another event.
The operation state machine is accepted -> started -> prepared -> effect_committed -> completed; a settled pre-preparation failure may go from started directly to effect_committed. The started event's durable receipt is required before started state and before any effect. Freeze the original started id. This rebuild never mutates canonical gists. Durable preparation, exact derived selection and effect_committed outcome/ref/hash follow the target protocol below; never substitute a candidate, infer success from mtime or repeat a committed swap. Recheck source revision and permission before effect; stale source records a settled failure without changing gists. The completed event appends only from effect_committed with its frozen succeeded/failed result. Its original receipt precedes completed row and terminal disclosure. If append succeeds but row advancement crashes, recover the stored original receipt and apply the same transition by CAS against exact prior row; failure before receipt cannot authorize a transition. Pending/ambiguous effect is unavailable until original owner recovery settles it. Event replay never runs maintenance. This family records only the acceptance transition; it may not be reinterpreted as completion.

The generic projector atomically CAS-advances complete rows and root frontier, never this reader. No new filtered durable cursor or projection value exists. Each read joins original source bytes, exact payload and operation/result custody, complete CURRENT-selected root/generation/frontier, original row birth anchor, actual permission/deletion/hold state. Recheck every fence after helpers and immediately before disclosure. Missing or stale authority returns unavailable; timestamps and cached views cannot substitute. Uses the ten-field live read token in its actual read transaction; any durable generic token is exactly SP-278/DL-076's nine fields, with redb_snapshot_id excluded. Reader output is ephemeral and never a persisted token. Generic checkpoint retains existing RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and index RP-EVENT-INDEX-SOURCE; missing derived state quarantines/rebuilds from retained source and never restores deleted gists.
Original operation/result, canonical gists, EventRecord and SP-286 receipts join coherent BRS-031 capture/restore boundaries; derived indexes are rebuilt, never backed up as canonical gists (DL-270). Ref resolution checks current Project access, source tombstones and holds on every read; ref/hash grants no access and body unavailability is disclosed without reconstructing content. Preserve original history and never retain deleted content inside audit metadata. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Unknown retention and operation-custody deletion remain pending, not an indefinite assignment.»
Only exact version 1.0.0 has this writer/reader; unknown or incompatible editions fail closed with original bytes preserved for authorized history. No implicit alias/migration. Withdrawal first fences new command acceptance and this family's writer admission, drains or explicitly leaves unresolved existing original operations without reissuing them, then under the same maintenance/read fence disables reader.memory.index.semantic.rebuild.started.history.v1@1.0.0 publication and invalidates live tokens. For memory.monthly_summary.started, memory.monthly_summary.completed, memory.prune_archive.started and memory.prune_archive.completed, each at 1.0.0, execute scripts/pm_memory_archive_events.py against Plans/memory_archive_event_fixtures.json. Each exact family adopts ATS-315 and the SP-636/SP-637 first-start-custody model by explicit SP-638/SP-639/CV-658/CV-659 adoption, not sibling admission. Test the closed separate payload and operation definitions, full EventRecord 2.0.0, encoded Project partition, storage-assigned retry-field exclusion, replay-only refusal, both terminal outcomes, CAS, start receipt on all writer/effect/recovery/history paths and SP-278 storage joins. Test cutoff refusal for automatic and direct invocation with no operation/effect/append/output; synthetic authority exercises the DL-446/DL-447 approved values without granting runtime admission. Historical originals stay readable with current cutoffs absent and source/request/counters changed, but forgery, access revocation and withdrawal refuse. Archive oracles compare selected originals in full except the allowed archived change, preserve all evidence refs/version refs and pins, and reject deletion/merging a pin. Cutoff lookup keys, resolved self-references and frozen operation refs must identify exactly one record; copied content hashes and all owner fields agree. A contradictory or ambiguous reference refuses despite coherent rehashing and intact start custody. Every negative is derived from an intact control; every refusal is a named guard-table row, and the shared guard tool cuts each row alone, requires its own negatives to flip and every other negative to keep its exact refusal, then restores it. A failed oracle must produce a nonzero process exit; unresolved refs including dormant branches fail. Bounds enforce 16 KiB and trailing LF rejection. Physical transactions, receipts, flushes and native execution are NOT_RUN. No admission or runtime activation is authorized by these tests.
Card 6 policy oracles execute scripts/pm_memory_policy.py through each exact --family checker using Plans/memory_card6_policy_fixtures.json. DL-444/DL-445 positives cover oldest creation time, same-time stable-ID tie, preserved evidence/merge history, archive-only copies and excluded pins. Negative post-states carry one semantic defect, with survivor-dependent archive/link/lineage copies changed coherently for a wrong-survivor case. DL-446/DL-447 positives and refusals cover 89/90 and 179/180 idle days, exact duration boundaries, scores 0.0999/0.10 and 0.0499/0.05, independent edit/access fallback, both conditions together, each Project separately and refusal of no-project execution. Each negative must produce only its named failed predicate; the full checker must exit nonzero on a wrong oracle. Round-11 preservation checks compare exact primitive types before values recursively, including selected and unselected originals, nested evidence/version/metadata values and full expected results. Dedup input flags must be exact Booleans; output flags must match exact Boolean originals or the explicitly permitted Boolean archived state. Boolean/integer aliases, typed floats, strings, null, arrays and objects have isolated one-field negatives. Eligible groups, selected IDs, embed_text_hash values and evidence references are exact-type checked before any value test, so aliases cannot read as one identical group or collapse in an evidence union. A malformed dedup or archive input or output refuses with its own named reason rather than raising, and the snapshot fields a job does not write (Project, eligible or selected IDs, capture time) must compare exactly. Full-checker wrong typed expected results must fail. Compare owner-admitted creation instants and elapsed idle durations with every fractional digit preserved, without truncation or a precision cap; retained timestamp spellings and commitments stay unchanged. Early, equal and late 90/180-day boundaries cover edit, access, creation fallback and capture at 9, 18 and 40 fractional digits; creation-order and stable-note-ID tie cases cover the same precisions. The dedup no-project input has coherent Project copies and a separate foreign-Project join negative. Minimum group size, unique IDs and original existence are separate guard-table rows, each with its own negative, proved by the shared guard tool. Snapshot usefulness scores remain owner-declared values outside integer identity recipes. No count cutoff, lane-local serializer or native proof is introduced. Existing number/format recipe issues are shared-sweep items, not repaired here. Source E-CARDS-2 as presented, Card 6 options A, SHA-256 6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30; decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md and ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md under /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104; DL-444 through DL-447, landed in Plans/Decision_Log.md on main.

claim_audit.text:
Newly authored owner contract under DL-045 for exactly memory.verification_sweep.completed@1.0.0; search scope and negative evidence are the family's row in reports/event-authority-20261104/DMEM-search.json. At preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, the family was absent from event_family_registry.json and quarantined before append or projection. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Retention is PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION: candidate ordinary telemetry (Case L-3, 90 days/2,000,000 per Project) versus audit authority (indefinite/no count eviction); neither is selected.» Unknown policy is materially incomplete and permits no destructive inference. Operation custody has the same pending assignment, and actual native activation is fenced until it resolves.
Identity recipe for this family: use strict UTF-8 canonical JSON of the array ["pm.memory.maintenance.event.v1",storage_instance_id,project_id,operation_id,"memory.verification_sweep.completed"] with no whitespace, ensure_ascii=false; SHA-256 lower hex. event_id="evt_mem_"+digest and idempotency_key="memory-maintenance:"+digest. All ids are nonempty bounded opaque owner-generated identifiers, not user content. The actual native acceptance generates operation_id once, persists it before publication and retries reuse it. request_sha256 binds the exact accepted command arguments and scope; a changed request under the same operation fails idempotency_conflict. Envelope type, payload type, project, correlation and causation must join CV-656.
Original operation custody is the newly authored memory_verification_sweep_operation family, closed schema Plans/memory_maintenance_operation.schema.json#/$defs/verification_sweep, key memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{hex(project_id)}:{hex(operation_id)} in canonical redb table memory_maintenance_operations. Hex is lowercase UTF-8 bytes, reversible and separator-safe. Admit its schema through the actual StorageMigrationCoordinator before any write, never inferred store versions. No duplicate command journal or gist store is created. Initial accepted row and request digest commit before append. This family explicitly adopts SP-286 and CV-339 full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody: validate admission, append barrier-class SeglogFrameV2 through SP-026/SP-236 with full flush, durably settle original receipt, then advance operation state. New issuance uses v2; resolve_full_value.v1 verifies the exact original event; missing/legacy-only proof fences dependent state. Lost delivery resolves the original receipt and cannot mint another event.
The operation state machine is accepted -> started -> effect_committed -> completed. The started event's durable receipt is required before started state and before any effect. Freeze the original started id. Canonical gist mutation and effect_committed outcome/ref/hash commit atomically in assistant_memory.redb under its single writer; partially applied sweeps resume only from recorded owner progress or roll back the transaction, never rerun committed merges or verification. Derived index rebuilds prepare a source-revision-bound shadow and durably record its exact target identity before swap; on recovery inspect that exact selected target and settle the same outcome under the maintenance lease, never republish a different target or infer success from mtime. Recheck source revision and permission before effect; stale source records a settled failure without changing gists. The completed event appends only from effect_committed with its frozen succeeded/failed result. Its original receipt precedes completed row and terminal disclosure. If append succeeds but row advancement crashes, recover the stored original receipt and apply the same transition by CAS against exact prior row; failure before receipt cannot authorize a transition. Pending/ambiguous effect is unavailable until original owner recovery settles it. Event replay never runs maintenance. This family records only the unique original terminal outcome; it cannot occur before the original start or be followed by another terminal result.
Exact consumer reader.memory.verification_sweep.completed.history.v1@1.0.0 is a newly authored stateless read-only binding used by Memory maintenance history and audit lookup for this exact type. It explicitly adopts SP-278: use reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 and projector.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0, checkpoint table checkpoints, key event_record_index_checkpoint.v1:{storage_instance_id}, closed value Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint, generation-qualified event_record_index.v2@{generation_id}. The generic projector atomically CAS-advances complete rows and root frontier, never this reader. No new filtered durable cursor or projection value exists. Each read joins original source bytes, exact payload and operation/result custody, complete CURRENT-selected root/generation/frontier, original row birth anchor, actual permission/deletion/hold state. Recheck every fence after helpers and immediately before disclosure. Missing or stale authority returns unavailable; timestamps and cached views cannot substitute. Uses the ten-field live read token in its actual read transaction; any durable generic token is exactly SP-278/DL-076's nine fields, with redb_snapshot_id excluded. Reader output is ephemeral and never a persisted token. Generic checkpoint retains existing RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and index RP-EVENT-INDEX-SOURCE; missing derived state quarantines/rebuilds from retained source and never restores deleted gists.
Original operation/result, canonical gists, EventRecord and SP-286 receipts join coherent BRS-031 capture/restore boundaries; derived indexes are rebuilt, never backed up as canonical gists (DL-270). Ref resolution checks current Project access, source tombstones and holds on every read; ref/hash grants no access and body unavailability is disclosed without reconstructing content. Preserve original history and never retain deleted content inside audit metadata. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Unknown retention and operation-custody deletion remain pending, not an indefinite assignment.»
Only exact version 1.0.0 has this writer/reader; unknown or incompatible editions fail closed with original bytes preserved for authorized history. No implicit alias/migration. Withdrawal first fences new command acceptance and this family's writer admission, drains or explicitly leaves unresolved existing original operations without reissuing them, then under the same maintenance/read fence disables reader.memory.verification_sweep.completed.history.v1@1.0.0 publication and invalidates live tokens. Generic index readers for other families continue. A successor must be explicitly admitted and rebuild from retained authenticated source with its own version; no withdrawn reader checkpoint can authorize effects. No event, policy, registry membership, readiness or native execution is admitted here.

claim_audit.text: Start custody gate for exactly memory.verification_sweep.completed@1.0.0, newly authored owner contract (DMEM fix round 4): the one rule behind every start-custody sentence in AMS-106, CV-656 and this SP-636. It adopts SP-286 and CV-339 first-AppendReceipt full-value custody and replaces none of their terms. Every path after first start admission goes through it: the completed append and its retry, the effect_committed to completed row CAS, the effect and its settlement, retry and replay of either retained original, recovery from every phase, the canonical current-writer append and retry, boundary acceptance and the history reader. Before such a path appends, CAS-publishes a row or selector, settles an effect, or returns or discloses an original, it resolves the exact original start record, the SP-286 retained full-value original of memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0 under this operation's memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1 key, authenticated through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1, and verifies all of: identity (event_id and idempotency_key recompute from the SP-637 recipe for this storage_instance_id, project_id and operation_id); digest (the retained full-value commitment recomputes from the retained value); operation (correlation_id and payload operation, Project, source revision, command and frozen start time equal the operation row); phase (the event type is exactly memory.verification_sweep.started and the row is accepted only before the start receipt, otherwise a later lawful phase); receipt (the first AppendReceipt settled under full flush, and the row's started_event_id and this event's causation_event_id and payload started_event_id name exactly that record); and no withdrawal fence on this family or memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0. Missing, corrupted, mismatched or withdrawn custody refuses with start_receipt_missing, or permission_or_withdrawal for a withdrawal fence, before any append, CAS, selector change, effect or output; the operation stays at its last durable phase and is never reissued. The gate is evaluated on the prior durable state and again on the tentative result immediately before commit, after any path-specific refusal, so no path, including one added later, can append, publish or return without it. The only relaxation belongs to memory.verification_sweep.started's own first append from an accepted row with no start receipt and no later original; no path of this family has it. Terminal custody stays the separate status/result/hash check above. The history reader returns a retained original that verified when written whatever the operation's current live state (later phase, source revision, selector, counters or request), and still refuses a withdrawal fence, revoked Project access, a forged or unverifiable original or missing start custody; it changes no state. Retention stays pending: this gate selects no retention period.

Every path after first start admission goes through it: the completed append and its retry, the effect_committed to completed row CAS, the effect and its settlement, retry and replay of either retained original, recovery from every phase, the canonical current-writer append and retry, boundary acceptance and the history reader. Before such a path appends, CAS-publishes a row or selector, settles an effect, or returns or discloses an original, it resolves the exact original start record, the SP-286 retained full-value original of memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0 under this operation's memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1 key, authenticated through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1, and verifies all of: identity (event_id and idempotency_key recompute from the SP-637 recipe for this storage_instance_id, project_id and operation_id); digest (the retained full-value commitment recomputes from the retained value); operation (correlation_id and payload operation, Project, source revision, command and frozen start time equal the operation row); phase (the event type is exactly memory.verification_sweep.started and the row is accepted only before the start receipt, otherwise a later lawful phase); receipt (the first AppendReceipt settled under full flush, and the row's started_event_id and this event's causation_event_id and payload started_event_id name exactly that record); and no withdrawal fence on this family or memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0. For memory.monthly_summary.started, memory.monthly_summary.completed, memory.prune_archive.started and memory.prune_archive.completed, each at 1.0.0, execute scripts/pm_memory_archive_events.py against Plans/memory_archive_event_fixtures.json. Each exact family adopts ATS-315 and the SP-636/SP-637 first-start-custody model by explicit SP-638/SP-639/CV-658/CV-659 adoption, not sibling admission. Test the closed separate payload and operation definitions, full EventRecord 2.0.0, encoded Project partition, storage-assigned retry-field exclusion, replay-only refusal, both terminal outcomes, CAS, start receipt on all writer/effect/recovery/history paths and SP-278 storage joins. Test cutoff refusal for automatic and direct invocation with no operation/effect/append/output; synthetic authority exercises the DL-446/DL-447 approved values without granting runtime admission. Historical originals stay readable with current cutoffs absent and source/request/counters changed, but forgery, access revocation and withdrawal refuse. Archive oracles compare selected originals in full except the allowed archived change, preserve all evidence refs/version refs and pins, and reject deletion/merging a pin. Cutoff lookup keys, resolved self-references and frozen operation refs must identify exactly one record; copied content hashes and all owner fields agree. A contradictory or ambiguous reference refuses despite coherent rehashing and intact start custody. Every negative is derived from an intact control; every refusal is a named guard-table row, and the shared guard tool cuts each row alone, requires its own negatives to flip and every other negative to keep its exact refusal, then restores it. A failed oracle must produce a nonzero process exit; unresolved refs including dormant branches fail. Bounds enforce 16 KiB and trailing LF rejection. Physical transactions, receipts, flushes and native execution are NOT_RUN. No admission or runtime activation is authorized by these tests.
Card 6 policy oracles execute scripts/pm_memory_policy.py through each exact --family checker using Plans/memory_card6_policy_fixtures.json. DL-444/DL-445 positives cover oldest creation time, same-time stable-ID tie, preserved evidence/merge history, archive-only copies and excluded pins. Negative post-states carry one semantic defect, with survivor-dependent archive/link/lineage copies changed coherently for a wrong-survivor case. DL-446/DL-447 positives and refusals cover 89/90 and 179/180 idle days, exact duration boundaries, scores 0.0999/0.10 and 0.0499/0.05, independent edit/access fallback, both conditions together, each Project separately and refusal of no-project execution. Each negative must produce only its named failed predicate; the full checker must exit nonzero on a wrong oracle. Round-11 preservation checks compare exact primitive types before values recursively, including selected and unselected originals, nested evidence/version/metadata values and full expected results. Dedup input flags must be exact Booleans; output flags must match exact Boolean originals or the explicitly permitted Boolean archived state. Boolean/integer aliases, typed floats, strings, null, arrays and objects have isolated one-field negatives. Eligible groups, selected IDs, embed_text_hash values and evidence references are exact-type checked before any value test, so aliases cannot read as one identical group or collapse in an evidence union. A malformed dedup or archive input or output refuses with its own named reason rather than raising, and the snapshot fields a job does not write (Project, eligible or selected IDs, capture time) must compare exactly. Full-checker wrong typed expected results must fail. Compare owner-admitted creation instants and elapsed idle durations with every fractional digit preserved, without truncation or a precision cap; retained timestamp spellings and commitments stay unchanged. Early, equal and late 90/180-day boundaries cover edit, access, creation fallback and capture at 9, 18 and 40 fractional digits; creation-order and stable-note-ID tie cases cover the same precisions. The dedup no-project input has coherent Project copies and a separate foreign-Project join negative. Minimum group size, unique IDs and original existence are separate guard-table rows, each with its own negative, proved by the shared guard tool. Snapshot usefulness scores remain owner-declared values outside integer identity recipes. No count cutoff, lane-local serializer or native proof is introduced. Existing number/format recipe issues are shared-sweep items, not repaired here. Source E-CARDS-2 as presented, Card 6 options A, SHA-256 6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30; decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md and ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md under /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104; DL-444 through DL-447, landed in Plans/Decision_Log.md on main.

The actual native acceptance generates operation_id once, persists it before publication and retries reuse it. request_sha256 binds the exact accepted command arguments and scope; a changed request under the same operation fails idempotency_conflict. Original operation custody is the newly authored memory_verification_sweep_operation family, closed schema Plans/memory_maintenance_operation.schema.json#/$defs/verification_sweep, key memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{hex(project_id)}:{hex(operation_id)} in canonical redb table memory_maintenance_operations. This family explicitly adopts SP-286 and CV-339 full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody: validate admission, append barrier-class SeglogFrameV2 through SP-026/SP-236 with full flush, durably settle original receipt, then advance operation state. Lost delivery resolves the original receipt and cannot mint another event.
The operation state machine is accepted -> started -> effect_committed -> completed. The started event's durable receipt is required before started state and before any effect. Freeze the original started id. Canonical gist mutation and effect_committed outcome/ref/hash commit atomically in assistant_memory.redb under its single writer; partially applied sweeps resume only from recorded owner progress or roll back the transaction, never rerun committed merges or verification. The completed event appends only from effect_committed with its frozen succeeded/failed result. Its original receipt precedes completed row and terminal disclosure. If append succeeds but row advancement crashes, recover the stored original receipt and apply the same transition by CAS against exact prior row; failure before receipt cannot authorize a transition. Pending/ambiguous effect is unavailable until original owner recovery settles it. Event replay never runs maintenance. This family records only the acceptance transition; it may not be reinterpreted as completion.

Recheck every fence after helpers and immediately before disclosure. Missing or stale authority returns unavailable; timestamps and cached views cannot substitute. Uses the ten-field live read token in its actual read transaction; any durable generic token is exactly SP-278/DL-076's nine fields, with redb_snapshot_id excluded. Reader output is ephemeral and never a persisted token. Generic checkpoint retains existing RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and index RP-EVENT-INDEX-SOURCE; missing derived state quarantines/rebuilds from retained source and never restores deleted gists.
Original operation/result, canonical gists, EventRecord and SP-286 receipts join coherent BRS-031 capture/restore boundaries; derived indexes are rebuilt, never backed up as canonical gists (DL-270). Ref resolution checks current Project access, source tombstones and holds on every read; ref/hash grants no access and body unavailability is disclosed without reconstructing content. Preserve original history and never retain deleted content inside audit metadata. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Unknown retention and operation-custody deletion remain pending, not an indefinite assignment.»
Only exact version 1.0.0 has this writer/reader; unknown or incompatible editions fail closed with original bytes preserved for authorized history. No implicit alias/migration. Withdrawal first fences new command acceptance and this family's writer admission, drains or explicitly leaves unresolved existing original operations without reissuing them, then under the same maintenance/read fence disables reader.memory.verification_sweep.started.history.v1@1.0.0 publication and invalidates live tokens. Every path after first start admission goes through it: retry of this family's first append, the accepted to started row CAS, the effect and its settlement, the terminal append and row CAS of memory.verification_sweep.completed, retry and replay of this original before and after completion, recovery from every phase, the canonical current-writer retry at every phase, boundary acceptance and the history reader. Before such a path appends, CAS-publishes a row or selector, settles an effect, or returns or discloses an original, it resolves the exact original start record, this family's own SP-286 retained full-value original under this operation's memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1 key; this event is the start record of its operation, authenticated through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1, and verifies all of: identity (event_id and idempotency_key recompute from this unit's recipe for this storage_instance_id, project_id and operation_id); digest (the retained full-value commitment recomputes from the retained value); operation (correlation_id and payload operation, Project, source revision, command and frozen start time equal the operation row); phase (the event type is exactly memory.verification_sweep.started and the row is accepted only before the start receipt, otherwise a later lawful phase); receipt (the first AppendReceipt settled under full flush, and the row's started_event_id and any retained memory.verification_sweep.completed original's causation_event_id and payload started_event_id name exactly that record); and no withdrawal fence on this family or memory.verification_sweep.completed@1.0.0. claim_audit.text:
For memory.monthly_summary.started, memory.monthly_summary.completed, memory.prune_archive.started and memory.prune_archive.completed, each at 1.0.0, execute scripts/pm_memory_archive_events.py against Plans/memory_archive_event_fixtures.json. Each exact family adopts ATS-315 and the SP-636/SP-637 first-start-custody model by explicit SP-638/SP-639/CV-658/CV-659 adoption, not sibling admission. Test the closed separate payload and operation definitions, full EventRecord 2.0.0, encoded Project partition, storage-assigned retry-field exclusion, replay-only refusal, both terminal outcomes, CAS, start receipt on all writer/effect/recovery/history paths and SP-278 storage joins. Test cutoff refusal for automatic and direct invocation with no operation/effect/append/output; synthetic authority exercises the DL-446/DL-447 approved values without granting runtime admission. Historical originals stay readable with current cutoffs absent and source/request/counters changed, but forgery, access revocation and withdrawal refuse. Archive oracles compare selected originals in full except the allowed archived change, preserve all evidence refs/version refs and pins, and reject deletion/merging a pin. Cutoff lookup keys, resolved self-references and frozen operation refs must identify exactly one record; copied content hashes and all owner fields agree. A contradictory or ambiguous reference refuses despite coherent rehashing and intact start custody. Every negative is derived from an intact control; every refusal is a named guard-table row, and the shared guard tool cuts each row alone, requires its own negatives to flip and every other negative to keep its exact refusal, then restores it. A failed oracle must produce a nonzero process exit; unresolved refs including dormant branches fail. Bounds enforce 16 KiB and trailing LF rejection. Physical transactions, receipts, flushes and native execution are NOT_RUN. No admission or runtime activation is authorized by these tests.
Card 6 policy oracles execute scripts/pm_memory_policy.py through each exact --family checker using Plans/memory_card6_policy_fixtures.json. DL-444/DL-445 positives cover oldest creation time, same-time stable-ID tie, preserved evidence/merge history, archive-only copies and excluded pins. Negative post-states carry one semantic defect, with survivor-dependent archive/link/lineage copies changed coherently for a wrong-survivor case. DL-446/DL-447 positives and refusals cover 89/90 and 179/180 idle days, exact duration boundaries, scores 0.0999/0.10 and 0.0499/0.05, independent edit/access fallback, both conditions together, each Project separately and refusal of no-project execution. Each negative must produce only its named failed predicate; the full checker must exit nonzero on a wrong oracle. Round-11 preservation checks compare exact primitive types before values recursively, including selected and unselected originals, nested evidence/version/metadata values and full expected results. Dedup input flags must be exact Booleans; output flags must match exact Boolean originals or the explicitly permitted Boolean archived state. Boolean/integer aliases, typed floats, strings, null, arrays and objects have isolated one-field negatives. Eligible groups, selected IDs, embed_text_hash values and evidence references are exact-type checked before any value test, so aliases cannot read as one identical group or collapse in an evidence union. A malformed dedup or archive input or output refuses with its own named reason rather than raising, and the snapshot fields a job does not write (Project, eligible or selected IDs, capture time) must compare exactly. Full-checker wrong typed expected results must fail. Compare owner-admitted creation instants and elapsed idle durations with every fractional digit preserved, without truncation or a precision cap; retained timestamp spellings and commitments stay unchanged. Early, equal and late 90/180-day boundaries cover edit, access, creation fallback and capture at 9, 18 and 40 fractional digits; creation-order and stable-note-ID tie cases cover the same precisions. The dedup no-project input has coherent Project copies and a separate foreign-Project join negative. Minimum group size, unique IDs and original existence are separate guard-table rows, each with its own negative, proved by the shared guard tool. Snapshot usefulness scores remain owner-declared values outside integer identity recipes. No count cutoff, lane-local serializer or native proof is introduced. Existing number/format recipe issues are shared-sweep items, not repaired here. Source E-CARDS-2 as presented, Card 6 options A, SHA-256 6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30; decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md and ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md under /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104; DL-444 through DL-447, landed in Plans/Decision_Log.md on main.

Withdrawal first fences this family's command/writer, retains unresolved original custody without reissue, then fences its exact reader and invalidates its live tokens under the same maintenance/read fence; other generic readers continue. A successor requires explicit admission and retained-source rebuild; no alias or migration by resemblance. Oracles are ATS-316 and scripts/pm_memory_archive_events.py, including positive conditional lifecycle, failed outcome, original retry, crash/recovery, historical independence, archive/evidence/pin negatives and guard-removal proof. Native execution is NOT_RUN. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Membership is ABSENT; no admission or readiness follows from this unit.» The started and completed payloads also require cutoff_ref and cutoff_sha256 exactly equal to the immutable operation fields, so start custody freezes the selected approval across recovery and retries.
Current producer-semantic projections and current identity inputs follow CV-1100 (current recipe cv1100-exact-integer-write-v3): every numeric leaf is an exact integer primitive, never a boolean, runtime float or fraction/exponent token, within the range its field owner schema declares; no global safe-integer ceiling applies, and raw input uses the CV-1100 current JSON integer grammar (scripts/pm_event_numbers.py loads_current_json), so 01, +1, -0, 1.0 and 1e0 are never read as integers. This producer route excludes Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc under Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord. Storage sequence_id independently adopts SP-236 exact uint64, 0 through 18446744073709551615 inclusive, with exact integer type; booleans, floats and strings refuse. Fresh writes and metadata-only retries preserve that full domain without a producer-number ceiling. Decimal and exponent tokens decode losslessly to exact decimal carriers before validation and are never folded into integers. Identity, idempotency, result and target commitments keep their local recipes, sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON over unchanged preimages, and admit only exact integers: a fraction, exponent or float spelling, a nonfinite value or an integer outside the range of its field owner refuses before hashing or append instead of being normalized. A current-writer retained EventRecord carries the unchanged CV-339 full-value commitment (pm.storage.original_event_value_commitment.v1 over the complete 2.0.0 EventRecord map in SP-236 EVENT_VALUE bytes, scripts/pm_event_numbers.py full_value_commitment) with exact Storage uint64 metadata; no new serializer is introduced. Historical originals instead use their frozen write-time recipe integer-json-v1: pm.event.v0 envelope editions 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 both retain their original unbounded integral sequence domains; operation/target edition 1.0.0 uses the explicit historical_ definitions frozen from 77323e87d65908dbce2ea655ee344b6185a13ff1, including artifact byte_length up to 9223372036854775807. The two frozen envelope editions share the integer-json-v1 numeric/hash recipe, and no record field, edition included, selects a recipe. Reader dispatch follows SP-1101: each retained canonical original (the writer's returned or canonical start original, a canonical history original and its start record, a checkpoint-joined original) resolves once through the shared RetainedDispatcher, which takes the write-time recipe tuple (envelope edition, writer recipe, full-value profile and resources) from Storage's sealed custody of that exact retained record, never from the record's schema_id/schema_version, a recipe field or the caller, and the composition-installed frozen verifier of that tuple then runs its checks. An original Storage did not seal at its seglog ref, one sealed with more than one binding or recipe, a sealed binding that is not the reader's, or a recipe with no installed verifier refuses at the site's custody guard; there is no current-then-legacy probing, permissive fallback or current writer predicate. The original full-value commitment is recomputed under that recipe with no rewrite of retained values, hashes, frozen operation or receipt. Historical numeric decoding preserves the original typed integer or binary64 stored value; a current lossless decimal parse never reinterprets an older binary64 original. Original verification in current-writer retries and checkpoint reader projections uses the sealed recipe of that original (CV-339 for a current-writer original, frozen integer-json-v1 for an older one); only the new caller producer-semantic projection and new-write producer admission use the strict current recipe; new caller Storage metadata is independently checked against SP-236. Valid retained large integers remain readable in canonical, replay-only, compatibility and compatibility-replay modes after live state/admission/cutoffs change; forged commitments, rehashed foreign values, unknown editions/recipe fields, lost custody, revoked permission and withdrawal still refuse. Plans/memory_maintenance_event_record.schema.json keeps SP-236 current Storage uint64 bounds (SP-1100, checked with storage_uint64), the producer_sequence_id domain of the EventRecord owner without an added ceiling, and unchanged frozen reader definitions; operation/target schemas keep current definitions and their frozen historical_ counterparts. Generic Storage metadata ownership is unchanged. Every declared date-time format is enforced by the shared CV-1101 predicate (scripts/pm_event_datetime.py date_time) with the explicit profile of its field owner, without optional validator packages: payload and EventRecord occurred_at_utc and the SP-278 checkpoint times take the broad event_record profile (RFC 3339 with an explicit zone, lowercase t or z, offsets, year 0000, any fraction length and announced leap seconds); Storage-assigned observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc take CV-253 storage_utc_z at the current and every retained envelope edition; the operation row's frozen started_occurred_at_utc and completed_occurred_at_utc keep their terminal-uppercase-Z owner pattern and take storage_utc_z. Bad calendar fields or separators, missing zones, an unannounced second 60 and trailing LF refuse, and a skipped old format check never authorizes invalid retained history. Existing length constraints remain. Timestamp strings retain their exact hash bytes. UUID uses the full 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal grammar. The selected recipe's frozen verifier applies the same profiles to retained originals; there is no narrower historical format edition.
Permission/admission and withdrawal fields, and every Boolean boundary receipt/source/acceptance fence, require the exact Boolean type before their value is evaluated; strings, numeric 0/1, null, arrays and objects never grant authority or clear a fence. Historical reads still use current typed permission/withdrawal only, not current admission or cutoffs.
Before archive selection and post-state validation, every resolved memory's pinned and archived fields in both input and output must have the exact Boolean type. A malformed flag refuses the whole settlement without state change or output; correctly typed pins and all original versions/EvidenceRefs retain the existing DL-402 preservation rules.

Ordering is by canonical source order, not timestamps. A complete survivor index can be fresh relative to verified survivors while `health=degraded`; loss provenance and global integrity/mutation fences remain. A reader pinned to an older coherent snapshot may finish only under the existing fence/lease; it cannot claim the latest boundary or disclose after invalidation.

claim_audit.text: **Compaction and crash convergence.** Build a complete target shadow under existing compaction intent/journal/lease and exact retained semantic set. The staged checkpoint is durably registered but never current. The old current node continues to win while CURRENT is proven unchanged. All target rows and staged frontier must be complete and mutually consistent before the existing synchronized CURRENT promotion. After CURRENT selects target, old index rows immediately cease to be current authority; startup activates the verified complete target shadow or rebuilds from target survivors.
