Newly authored owner contract under DL-045 for exactly memory.verification_sweep.completed@1.0.0; search scope and negative evidence are the family's row in reports/event-authority-20261104/DMEM-search.json. At preparation before the 2026-11-18 registration, the family was absent from event_family_registry.json and quarantined before append or projection. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Retention is PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION: candidate ordinary telemetry (Case L-3, 90 days/2,000,000 per Project) versus audit authority (indefinite/no count eviction); neither is selected.» Unknown policy is materially incomplete and permits no destructive inference. Operation custody has the same pending assignment, and actual native activation is fenced until it resolves.
Identity recipe for this family: use strict UTF-8 canonical JSON of the array ["pm.memory.maintenance.event.v1",storage_instance_id,project_id,operation_id,"memory.verification_sweep.completed"] with no whitespace, ensure_ascii=false; SHA-256 lower hex. event_id="evt_mem_"+digest and idempotency_key="memory-maintenance:"+digest. All ids are nonempty bounded opaque owner-generated identifiers, not user content. The actual native acceptance generates operation_id once, persists it before publication and retries reuse it. request_sha256 binds the exact accepted command arguments and scope; a changed request under the same operation fails idempotency_conflict. Envelope type, payload type, project, correlation and causation must join CV-656.
Original operation custody is the newly authored memory_verification_sweep_operation family, closed schema Plans/memory_maintenance_operation.schema.json#/$defs/verification_sweep, key memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{hex(project_id)}:{hex(operation_id)} in canonical redb table memory_maintenance_operations. Hex is lowercase UTF-8 bytes, reversible and separator-safe. Admit its schema through the actual StorageMigrationCoordinator before any write, never inferred store versions. No duplicate command journal or gist store is created. Initial accepted row and request digest commit before append. This family explicitly adopts SP-286 and CV-339 full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody: validate admission, append barrier-class SeglogFrameV2 through SP-026/SP-236 with full flush, durably settle original receipt, then advance operation state. New issuance uses v2; resolve_full_value.v1 verifies the exact original event; missing/legacy-only proof fences dependent state. Lost delivery resolves the original receipt and cannot mint another event.
The operation state machine is accepted -> started -> effect_committed -> completed. The started event's durable receipt is required before started state and before any effect. Freeze the original started id. Canonical gist mutation and effect_committed outcome/ref/hash commit atomically in assistant_memory.redb under its single writer; partially applied sweeps resume only from recorded owner progress or roll back the transaction, never rerun committed merges or verification. Derived index rebuilds prepare a source-revision-bound shadow and durably record its exact target identity before swap; on recovery inspect that exact selected target and settle the same outcome under the maintenance lease, never republish a different target or infer success from mtime. Recheck source revision and permission before effect; stale source records a settled failure without changing gists. The completed event appends only from effect_committed with its frozen succeeded/failed result. Its original receipt precedes completed row and terminal disclosure. If append succeeds but row advancement crashes, recover the stored original receipt and apply the same transition by CAS against exact prior row; failure before receipt cannot authorize a transition. Pending/ambiguous effect is unavailable until original owner recovery settles it. Event replay never runs maintenance. This family records only the unique original terminal outcome; it cannot occur before the original start or be followed by another terminal result.
Exact consumer reader.memory.verification_sweep.completed.history.v1@1.0.0 is a newly authored stateless read-only binding used by Memory maintenance history and audit lookup for this exact type. It explicitly adopts SP-278: use reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 and projector.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0, checkpoint table checkpoints, key event_record_index_checkpoint.v1:{storage_instance_id}, closed value Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint, generation-qualified event_record_index.v2@{generation_id}. The generic projector atomically CAS-advances complete rows and root frontier, never this reader. No new filtered durable cursor or projection value exists. Each read joins original source bytes, exact payload and operation/result custody, complete CURRENT-selected root/generation/frontier, original row birth anchor, actual permission/deletion/hold state. Recheck every fence after helpers and immediately before disclosure. Missing or stale authority returns unavailable; timestamps and cached views cannot substitute. Uses the ten-field live read token in its actual read transaction; any durable generic token is exactly SP-278/DL-076's nine fields, with redb_snapshot_id excluded. Reader output is ephemeral and never a persisted token. Generic checkpoint retains existing RP-PROJECTION-3GEN and index RP-EVENT-INDEX-SOURCE; missing derived state quarantines/rebuilds from retained source and never restores deleted gists.
Original operation/result, canonical gists, EventRecord and SP-286 receipts join coherent BRS-031 capture/restore boundaries; derived indexes are rebuilt, never backed up as canonical gists (DL-270). Ref resolution checks current Project access, source tombstones and holds on every read; ref/hash grants no access and body unavailability is disclosed without reconstructing content. Preserve original history and never retain deleted content inside audit metadata. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, stale wording in received dfea17a6c4): «Unknown retention and operation-custody deletion remain pending, not an indefinite assignment.»
Only exact version 1.0.0 has this writer/reader; unknown or incompatible editions fail closed with original bytes preserved for authorized history. No implicit alias/migration. Withdrawal first fences new command acceptance and this family's writer admission, drains or explicitly leaves unresolved existing original operations without reissuing them, then under the same maintenance/read fence disables reader.memory.verification_sweep.completed.history.v1@1.0.0 publication and invalidates live tokens. Generic index readers for other families continue. A successor must be explicitly admitted and rebuild from retained authenticated source with its own version; no withdrawn reader checkpoint can authorize effects. No event, policy, registry membership, readiness or native execution is admitted here.

claim_audit.text: Start custody gate for exactly memory.verification_sweep.completed@1.0.0, newly authored owner contract (DMEM fix round 4): the one rule behind every start-custody sentence in AMS-106, CV-656 and this SP-636. It adopts SP-286 and CV-339 first-AppendReceipt full-value custody and replaces none of their terms. Every path after first start admission goes through it: the completed append and its retry, the effect_committed to completed row CAS, the effect and its settlement, retry and replay of either retained original, recovery from every phase, the canonical current-writer append and retry, boundary acceptance and the history reader. Before such a path appends, CAS-publishes a row or selector, settles an effect, or returns or discloses an original, it resolves the exact original start record, the SP-286 retained full-value original of memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0 under this operation's memory_verification_sweep_operation.v1 key, authenticated through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1, and verifies all of: identity (event_id and idempotency_key recompute from the SP-637 recipe for this storage_instance_id, project_id and operation_id); digest (the retained full-value commitment recomputes from the retained value); operation (correlation_id and payload operation, Project, source revision, command and frozen start time equal the operation row); phase (the event type is exactly memory.verification_sweep.started and the row is accepted only before the start receipt, otherwise a later lawful phase); receipt (the first AppendReceipt settled under full flush, and the row's started_event_id and this event's causation_event_id and payload started_event_id name exactly that record); and no withdrawal fence on this family or memory.verification_sweep.started@1.0.0. Missing, corrupted, mismatched or withdrawn custody refuses with start_receipt_missing, or permission_or_withdrawal for a withdrawal fence, before any append, CAS, selector change, effect or output; the operation stays at its last durable phase and is never reissued. The gate is evaluated on the prior durable state and again on the tentative result immediately before commit, after any path-specific refusal, so no path, including one added later, can append, publish or return without it. The only relaxation belongs to memory.verification_sweep.started's own first append from an accepted row with no start receipt and no later original; no path of this family has it. Terminal custody stays the separate status/result/hash check above. The history reader returns a retained original that verified when written whatever the operation's current live state (later phase, source revision, selector, counters or request), and still refuses a withdrawal fence, revoked Project access, a forged or unverifiable original or missing start custody; it changes no state. Retention stays pending: this gate selects no retention period.

Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. New create preserves the absent or complete source evidence in its original request; duplicate requires all three source fields.

Application requires scope_kind=application, scope_partition=app and required-present null project_id/project_home_server_id/named_plan_id. Project requires the actual nonempty Project/Home Server, scope_partition=project~ plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id under existing Storage §2.2.5, and a real named_plan_id only when actually referenced, otherwise null. Empty/sentinel Project strings, mismatched outer/inner scope and focus-based inference refuse. Before first message use draft_id, never a fabricated durable thread.

Default/Computer Settings, settings.follow and client reachability grant no Project/content/execution authority. The existing owner durably binds its fresh 128-bit operation_id and input digest before effect, commits the original authorized whole-record/selection/export result and readback, then prepares `persona_created_operation.v1:<storage_instance_id>:<scope_key>:<operation_id>` before event append. Missing original completion remains pending; no cross-store atomicity is assumed. New key scope_key is compact UTF-8 JSON `[server_id, scope_partition]` from the original request, so different real Servers cannot share app keys. Preserve original operation_id, source/result receipt, actor, revision and timestamp; one key with different input/semantic bytes conflicts. An observing retry may not mint a source operation or repeat its effect. Observe only the successful created result of cmd.persona.create, or duplicated result of cmd.persona.duplicate. PERSONA.md validates before the whole definition is committed and read back at its chosen home. No-project create chooses Your library; a Project version requires an actual Project. Duplicate uses a new non-reserved persona_id and exact source ID/revision/hash; it is not the same-ID save-as-override action. Protected IDs and folder/ID mismatch refuse before effect. New create preserves the absent or complete source evidence in its original request; duplicate requires all three source fields.

claim_audit.text: Consumer **`consumer.persona_created.history@1.0.0`** serves the existing authenticated Persona command/audit history only. No new filtered projection or checkpoint is owned. Index-row/frontier publication is the generic atomic CAS with source/prefix/gap/rebuild fences. Filter exact `persona.created`/1.0.0, owning Server and original scope after whole-token verification. Revalidate retained source availability and current read permissions for the original home/reach, redaction and deletion/tombstone before disclosure; forged/withdrawn/missing retained source is unavailable. Replay/rebuild only indexes retained authenticated events and never invokes `handlers::persona::create (or the existing handlers::persona::duplicate distinct-ID route)` or resolves historical runtime identity anew. Historical reads of `persona.created` validate the immutable event and frozen original at-write admission/source/result/receipt evidence, plus current consumer admission, access, redaction, body availability and withdrawal fences. Later account disconnect, plugin unload, Persona update/deletion, CAS/revision or selection changes, or expiration of the current writer/definition lease do not invalidate an otherwise retained event that was valid when written. Current live state is a separate input and cannot replace frozen provenance. Forged/unadmitted-at-write or withdrawn family/consumer events remain refused; a deleted/unavailable body is not disclosed. Reading never invokes a producer or grants present execution authority.

claim_audit.text: The sole producer `handlers::persona::delete` authenticates the selected command input/result and actual home/reach/CAS/permission/Stop generations before effect and immediately before append. Separate writer/schema/retention admission is mandatory; preparation grants none and required unadmitted event writers block their effects. The existing owner durably binds its fresh 128-bit operation_id and input digest before effect, commits the original authorized whole-record/selection/export result and readback, then prepares `persona_deleted_operation.v1:<storage_instance_id>:<scope_key>:<operation_id>` before event append. Missing original completion remains pending; no cross-store atomicity is assumed. New key scope_key is compact UTF-8 JSON `[server_id, scope_partition]` from the original request, so different real Servers cannot share app keys. Preserve original operation_id, source/result receipt, actor, revision and timestamp; one key with different input/semantic bytes conflicts. An observing retry may not mint a source operation or repeat its effect. Observe only the confirmed deleted result of cmd.persona.delete for the exact mutable whole version at expected_owner_revision. A protected core built-in cannot be deleted. Deleting an eligible Project version removes only that version and reveals the library version, as P-060 and section 4.1 specify; deleting the library record follows the existing owner rule. Capture the original removed revision/hash and readback receipt, never invent a replacement Persona or body lifetime. Event history is metadata, not authority to delete linked content or other versions.

No cross-store atomicity is claimed. Auth credentials remain solely in the OS store. Plugin source receipts remain sole operational authority.

One key cannot be reused for another input. Pending work fences conflicting work for that subject. The existing owner effect/body and authenticated result receipt precede this observation record and the event; unavailable owner completion stays pending, never guessed or repeated. No cross-store atomicity is claimed. Auth credentials remain solely in the OS store. Plugin source receipts remain sole operational authority.

claim_audit.text: The sole producer `plugin loader failure handler` first validates actual source/permission/receipt ownership, the closed payload and installed writer/schema/retention admission. The existing source owner allocates and durably binds operation_id before its side effect, keeping that ID in original typed-result custody. After the original effect and its result receipt are committed, and before event append, durably prepare `plugin_load_failed_operation.v1:<storage_instance_id>:<scope_key>:<operation_id>` with exact authenticated result, actor and original source receipt. The Event ID recipe retains scope_key=`application` for application or `project:<project_id>` for Project from original receipt custody. This recipe component is not the storage partition: actual storage scope_partition is `app` or `project~` plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id. Independently retain the actual original server_id in the closed operation and authenticate it against the original typed result; focus, a caller assertion or a borrowed receipt cannot supply it. WorkflowScopeV2 supplies the closed source scope; envelope Project and original scope must agree. Operation IDs are fresh 128-bit entropy persisted by the source owner before effect and recovered from the same original receipt, never minted anew by an observing retry; revisions and timestamps are frozen. One key cannot be reused for another input. Pending work fences conflicting work for that subject. The existing owner effect/body and authenticated result receipt precede this observation record and the event; unavailable owner completion stays pending, never guessed or repeated. No cross-store atomicity is claimed. Auth credentials remain solely in the OS store. Plugin source receipts remain sole operational authority.

claim_audit.text: The sole producer `hook error/timeout result handler` first validates actual source/permission/receipt ownership, the closed payload and installed writer/schema/retention admission. The existing source owner allocates and durably binds operation_id before its side effect, keeping that ID in original typed-result custody. After the original effect and its result receipt are committed, and before event append, durably prepare `plugin_hook_error_operation.v1:<storage_instance_id>:<scope_key>:<operation_id>` with exact authenticated result, actor and original source receipt. The Event ID recipe retains scope_key=`application` for application or `project:<project_id>` for Project from original receipt custody. This recipe component is not the storage partition: actual storage scope_partition is `app` or `project~` plus unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id. Independently retain the actual original server_id in the closed operation and authenticate it against the original typed result; focus, a caller assertion or a borrowed receipt cannot supply it. WorkflowScopeV2 supplies the closed source scope; envelope Project and original scope must agree. Operation IDs are fresh 128-bit entropy persisted by the source owner before effect and recovered from the same original receipt, never minted anew by an observing retry; revisions and timestamps are frozen. One key cannot be reused for another input. Pending work fences conflicting work for that subject. The existing owner effect/body and authenticated result receipt precede this observation record and the event; unavailable owner completion stays pending, never guessed or repeated. No cross-store atomicity is claimed. Auth credentials remain solely in the OS store. Plugin source receipts remain sole operational authority.

Producer: PreviewSession owner consumes cmd.orchestrator.preview_stop and records actual runtime closure as runtime_state closed after managed resources settle. UI restore intent stays subject-owned; stop does not change build/run state. A closed/historical session cannot stop again on replay; browser overlay closure, where required, remains BrowserRuntimeService-owned.
Scope: project_only; EventRecord.project_id equals actual payload.project_id; EventRecord.run_id equals payload.run_id when linked and is null when no actual Run is linked. Optional thread/terminal/DAP/browser ids are actual owner joins, never guessed or invented.
Identity: stable original event_id allocated once; Idempotency key is sha256(canonical MessagePack array ["preview.session.stopped", "1.0.0", actual project_id, preview_subject_id, preview_session_id, preview_revision]). Changed bytes at the same identity refuse. Revisions track actual committed owner transitions, never delivery attempts. Resolve cross-owner identity and current permission at admission and again at final publication.
Payload: Plans/ds15_preview_session_stopped.schema.json is the exact closed 1.0.0 payload. Only bounded identifiers and opaque owner-resolved non-secret refs: no page/DOM, local absolute paths, cookies, config bodies, credentials, screenshot bytes, command arguments or raw output.
Ordering and custody: explicitly adopt SP-286 / CV-339 full-value v2 successor and Case L-2/SP-026/SP-236 ordinary SeglogFrameV2 append/read. Check current exact family admission/producer/codec/source and original input custody before work; registry absence fences production only when this exact family/selected version is actually absent. Commit the authentic owner outcome first, freeze its complete immutable result/event identity, append through the single writer, retain original first AppendReceipt and frozen full value under SP-286, then publish success or terminal result. An interrupted owner outcome is not reconstructed from current UI state. Missing or ambiguous original outcome stays fenced.
Replay: lost acknowledgement returns original receipt, event_id and frozen payload; retry uses original outcome custody without repeating capture, thread creation, launch, stop, restart or refresh. If original outcome exists but append/receipt is unresolved, inspect single-writer dedupe and recover append using original identity; no new effect. SP-286 stores frozen transition outcome/receipt, not a new DS15 receipt family.
Consumer: reader.ds15.preview_session_stopped.v1@1.0.0, operating as Preview subject history reader, reads only preview.session.stopped@1.0.0. It adopts SP-278 by name and DL-076 nine-field durable token. Checkpoint key projector.checkpoint.ds15.preview_session_stopped:{project_id}, value Plans/ds15_preview_session_stopped_checkpoint.schema.json. Capture CURRENT-selected complete generic-index coverage, scan the whole selected global sequence range in order with exact family and actual scope filter, and CAS complete prior checkpoint plus new value in one redb transaction. through_sequence_id is last globally scanned sequence, last_event_id last matching event; no checkpoint until first match. Gaps, omitted matches, partial scan, changed source/token/live snapshot/access/deletion/reader or stale full previous value preserve prior checkpoint. Rejoin live redb_snapshot_id at each read/advance/recovery; never persist it. Rebuild captures fresh complete retained source; missing prefix is unavailable, never reset to zero or claimed current. Resolve original event refs for history; replay never replays user actions.
Redaction/custody: original seglog/first-receipt owner keeps original event bytes; source owners keep original composer/workflow/preview outcomes and refs with verified coherent backup/restore of the full original source/log/receipt closure. Checkpoints are derived and grant no access. Every read rechecks current subject/thread/Project permissions and source deletion/tombstones before disclosure; denied/deleted sources return unavailable without copying content into history.
Value binding: SP-656/CV-676 and Plans/ds15_preview_state_v2.schema.json bind subject-keyed UI/restore state separately from live preview_session_id and optional browser_session_id. No cached running value is liveness proof. Legacy preview_id mapping requires owner-verified subject identity and keeps historical runtime state; ambiguous identity refuses migration. Restore intent is reconstructed through existing owner policy; it grants no automation resume or browser launch authority.
Historical preparation status (2026-11-18 snapshot at 0f2a90ece5; superseded by the current assignment below): Retention: retention_policy_ref = PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION for event and checkpoint. RT candidates are Case L-3 chat content for capture, Runtime/run/node/attempt only when an actual Run exists, approval/receipt/audit authority, or ordinary telemetry; no assignment/expiry/deletion is selected. Do not admit until RT resolves both. Existing value policies remain where unchanged; a broadened schema is held for RT rather than extending a DAP policy to workflow content.
Compatibility and withdrawal: exact 1.0.0 event/reader only; refuse unknown fields/version before effects or checkpoint. No alias or deployed event predecessor is assumed. Value migrations are explicit coordinator transactions with source backup, validation, owner joins, complete codec verification and store version written last, never lazy rewrite-on-read. Withdrawal fences new writer admissions at committed source frontier under coordinator exclusion, drains original admitted results/receipts, then fences reader/checkpoint advance. In-flight old-reader CAS fails. Mark existing checkpoint withdrawn; preserve canonical originals under their owner policies. Reinstall requires current owner authorization and a fresh SP-278 complete rebuild, never old permission/publication authority.
Oracles: ATS-329 and exact family cases in Plans/ds15_event_contract_fixtures.json execute via scripts/pm-ds15-event-contracts.py: valid/invalid transition, scope joins, original receipt/outcome recovery, no repeat effect, full coverage/CAS, permission/deletion, rebuild and writer/reader withdrawal. Versioned value cases use Plans/ds15_value_contract_fixtures.json. Static reference models prove no native behavior; native execution NOT_RUN.

Bind the actual storage instance and app or Storage-encoded project~base64url partition to the complete original EventRecord. Retry equality compares only the CV-317 producer-supplied semantic fields and stable event_id, excluding Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc; original full-value custody still commits those original fields immutably. Final publication rechecks current owner authorization, permission, deletion and applicable sharing; denial preserves receipt custody and never reruns the old effect. Pure retained-receipt resolution remains independent of retired source controls under SP-286. Bind scan low/high and every global row to independently verified CURRENT-selected complete source and its exact storage/token identity. A complete later suffix with zero family matches advances the global frontier while retaining the verified prior last_event_id; before the first match no checkpoint exists. SP-337 caps inline body at 16384 bytes; larger content stays in owner-resolved payload references with BLAKE3 id, size and media type, never an enlarged inline body. Identifier patterns require an actual full match, including trailing-LF rejection. These static oracles grant no native proof; NOT_RUN remains.
Round 7 authenticated history for preview.session.stopped: retained read, checkpoint and rebuild accept supported 1.0.0 originals written with projector_replay_only as well as dedupe_by_idempotency_key. Only current writes/retries enforce replay_only_not_appendable. Authenticate original payload/version and original transition against retained original_context, complete committed outcome, coherent backup closure and SP-286 full-value receipt on every path, before checkpoint equality/advance. Current live transition state is not original authority; current exact-boolean owner authorization, disclosure, source deletion, sharing and withdrawal still fence every historical read/advance. Every selected matching global-index row resolves its own original event/receipt/source and must agree on event_id, event_type, actual scope, scope_partition and Storage-assigned sequence; missing or contradictory sources preserve the prior checkpoint. Authority context is closed by the exact family definition in Plans/ds15_authority_context.schema.json. Check exact boolean and bounded integer types before interpreting flags, comparing revisions/frontiers or hashing. Malformed values refuse with zero effects, never an uncaught comparison exception. All eleven standing checks and item-11 type probes are executable, not inferred from schema syntax.
Round 7 type/source refinement: original_context retains the complete writer transition schema; retained read/checkpoint/rebuild require only current scope and exact-boolean owner authorization, plus the existing disclosure/deletion/share/withdrawal fences. They do not require disposed live transition controls. Plans/ds15_index_inputs.schema.json closes the independent selected global source rows before partition/sequence work. Checkpoint schema/byte validation is the shared checkpoint_value_ok used by actual advance and the static checkpoint_boundary oracle; the boundary grants no advance or append authority.
Round 7 closed evidence carrier: Plans/ds15_original_evidence.schema.json validates original/outcome wrappers, source-map shape and exact carrier metadata types before interpretation; only fields consumed by the operation are required. Original source controls remain frozen, and retained current disclosure context needs only actual subject scope and exact owner authorization. Every envelope joins the complete requested subject scope to the authenticated payload namespace. Candidate semantic body equality is checked before identity/hash construction. Unchanged checkpoint/rebuild results also verify complete selected source and each original Storage join. Pure stored receipt recovery still does not require disposed live transition controls. These are newly authored technical validation bindings, not a native admission.

A refused event appends nothing and changes no row.

claim_audit.text: **Replay, rebuild and withdrawal.** Replay runs in canonical seglog order from the checkpoint's inclusive cursor and only rebuilds projection rows: no message delivery, dispatch, card, notification, command or append follows from replay. Missing, malformed or inconsistent rows or checkpoint enter the existing Q-DERIVED quarantine and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds them from verified CURRENT-selected source through the adopted SP-278 token; readers get unavailable meanwhile. `admitted_event_types` grows only through a governed rebuild: the current core is withdrawn, the projector rebuilds over the complete range with the new set and a new core is published; admitting a family never back-fills, aliases or re-reads a sibling. Withdrawal of one family: first the writer is cut off (the append admission refuses it, and the runtime refuses whatever its unit says depends on it); then the current core is withdrawn with `withdrawn_at_utc` set once, the projector stops ordinary advance and readers return unavailable; last, every original event and its dedupe and receipt custody are kept, the owner-approved successor is identified, and StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuilds with the new admitted set before a new core is published. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion follows. A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

A run that cannot reach an admitted terminal event stays non-terminal in the projection and is never inferred terminal.

This exact family implements only the existing Option 2 transition: A summary-only reasoning artifact becomes durable; private chain-of-thought or raw hidden reasoning is not captured.
The producer is Agent summary writer, through the newly named handler owner.runtime_artifacts.reasoning_summary.publish@1.0.0. This handler seals one immutable artifact metadata record; it does not perform the source operation. Validate the closed schema Plans/runtime_artifact_reasoning_summary.schema.json (pm.runtime_artifact.reasoning_summary.schema.v1) and current producer/read permission before commit. Project root edition only: nonempty payload.project_id must equal the canonical CV-317 envelope project_id, scope_kind=project; artifact_type=reasoning_summary, schema_id=pm.runtime_artifact.reasoning_summary.schema.v1. All run/attempt/thread/node/provider/usage refs must resolve to that same owning Project and original source; absent optional refs never inherit focused UI identity. Non-restore artifacts require original run_id and attempt_id. Application successor definitions in CV-366/SP-349/351/352 are separate source/key graphs and are not written into this Project edition; this draft changes none of them.
Identity adopts the owner-recommended four-member tuple exactly: [event_type, project_id, artifact_id, schema_id]. Each member is encoded as uint32 big-endian UTF-8 byte length followed by its exact UTF-8 bytes, in that order, without normalization; reject length overflow. idempotency_key is "ra1:" plus lowercase SHA-256 of those framed bytes. EventRecord event_id is allocated once by Storage on first accepted append and thereafter returned from original custody; only sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc are Storage assignments; occurred_at_utc preserves the original producer-authored payload.created_at_utc. Matching identity with changed producer-semantic payload is a conflict, never an overwrite. No timestamp, summary, preview or subtype is an identity substitute.
The producer validates and durably commits any required referenced body through its existing source owner, then freezes the exact metadata payload. The EventRecord append is the first canonical persistence of artifact metadata; no second metadata or pending-request value is introduced. It then uses ordinary Case L-2 SeglogFrameV2 append with the exact identity, explicitly adopting SP-286/CV-339 and the installed full-value v2 successor including storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1. First receipt issuance is the group's durable commit frame under SP-336/SP-347; the custody transaction follows sync. No terminal artifact publication precedes authentic first-receipt custody and the final source/permission guard. No durable pending-request family is invented. After crash, retry only from the same authentic sealed source identity; no redispatch of its source action. If the original source or receipt cannot be proven, report unavailable and fence publication. Lost acknowledgements return the original EventRecord/receipt through actual first-receipt resolution; replay cannot manufacture a new event_id, body, receipt or external effect.
The exact passive operating consumer is reader.runtime_artifacts.reasoning_summary.history@1.0.0, for the already specified artifact evidence/history inspection path. It consumes complete EventRecord 2.0.0 source values through reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 and explicitly adopts SP-278. It returns only verified original metadata and authorized refs, never dispatches actions, appends siblings or fills a missing original from a projection. The artifact index and panel projection remain independently deferred; this history reader neither enables nor redefines them.
Retain this event, including embedded summary/text and original provenance, under RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE@1.0.0 (DL-075 and Case L-3). The payload retention_class describes the artifact/body policy, never the EventRecord policy. Artifact bodies, Usage, original receipts and other source records retain their own existing policies; deleting a linked body does not erase event-embedded text. On each read recheck current authorization, source deletion/revocation and holds; inaccessible bodies remain unavailable and are never reconstructed from the retained event. No new deletion exception or preservation hold is created. Seglog owns original event custody, coherent backup and restore; include original EventRecord and SP-286 receipt custody from the same verified store/source selection. A derived index is not a backup of either. Redact before sealing; refs and summaries must not carry secrets, private reasoning, protected auth-session captures or raw hidden content.
Compatibility is exact-version only: unsupported schema IDs/versions fail closed with unsupported_schema_version. Existing source-lineage values may be inspected only through their explicitly supported decoder and original provenance, never rewritten as current events. Withdrawal first closes this exact producer's admission under the owner writer lease and drains or fences in-flight publication; preserve original issued receipts and events. Stop this reader before withdrawing its installed SP-278 dependency, invalidate its ephemeral view, then reinstall a versioned compatible reader and perform a complete authorized source read. Rebuild never republishes an event or source operation. No registry entry, native dispatch, PNC-019 or readiness follows this contract.
Only the agent-authored visible summary may be sealed. No private chain-of-thought or raw hidden reasoning is admitted.

claim_audit.text:
Newly authored Storage adoption for runtime_artifact.reasoning_summary@1.0.0 only. owner.runtime_artifacts.reasoning_summary.publish@1.0.0 and reader.runtime_artifacts.reasoning_summary.history@1.0.0 adopt the exact identity, commit/append/receipt barriers, immutable original custody, replay and withdrawal of RAP-112; no admission is performed.
Reuse projector.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 and reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 under SP-278, not the deferred runtime_artifact_projector_families row. The exact physical checkpoint is event_record_index_checkpoint.v1:{storage_instance_id} in the checkpoints table; value pm.storage_value.event_record_index_checkpoint.v1@1.0.0 at Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint, canonical MessagePack. Its actual current_generation_id selects event_record_index.v2@{generation_id} and checkpoint_ref points to #/generations/{generation_id}. Existing index and checkpoint registry rows already own those values. No new stored value, filtered checkpoint, projection key or compatibility alias is allocated by this family.
reader.runtime_artifacts.reasoning_summary.history@1.0.0 is stateless across calls. It acquires one current SP-278 read token and reads the complete requested Project partition range against actual canonical frames through that captured frontier, filtering event_type=runtime_artifact.reasoning_summary only after examining the complete range. It verifies source selection, generation membership, payload hash, envelope joins and original source authority. Malformed, unknown, missing, wrong-Project or corrupt values fail the view; they never count as covered gaps. Return captured bounds/currentness and actual gaps; no timestamp approximation or mixed-generation pagination. Revalidate current selection and permissions before returning. No family-local durable advance occurs. The adopted full-index projector advances rows and frontier atomically in one redb transaction with prior-generation/frontier CAS, as SP-278 requires. The live token has ten fields; any durable copy must use DL-076's nine fields, excluding redb_snapshot_id. This consumer persists neither token nor view.
The reused event_record_index rows retain RP-EVENT-INDEX-SOURCE, source-coupled to the retained EventRecord, with complete target-generation rebuild/remapping at compaction. Only event_record_index_checkpoint generation history uses RP-PROJECTION-3GEN under SP-278: current plus at most two other generations, retirement/hold/reference fences and governed rebuild. Restore/rebuild uses verified CURRENT-selected seglog and authentic receipt custody; never copy an old derived checkpoint into current authority. Missing or corrupt checkpoint is unavailable pending StorageMigrationCoordinator rebuild; actual schema/table installation precedes reading. Canonical event history retains RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE under DL-075, including embedded text, independently of artifact-body policies. Explicitly adopt SP-286 full-value v2 and storage.first_append_receipt.resolve_full_value.v1 for original result recovery; dedupe locators alone are not original receipt authority.
This exact family changes no artifacts_index/artifacts_project_state/checkpoint.runtime_artifacts physical disposition, grants no action, and never claims that a source-index checkpoint proves a panel projection is current. Native storage, codec, backup, CAS, crash and UI proof remain NOT_RUN.

Newly authored owner contract under DL-045 for runtime_artifact.restore_point@1.0.0, prepared without admission. This exact family implements only the existing Option 2 transition: A restore-point record becomes durable or changes its recorded availability/lifecycle state under the existing field-deep contract.
The producer is Restore-point owner observation writer, through the newly named handler owner.runtime_artifacts.restore_point.publish@1.0.0. This handler seals one immutable artifact metadata record; it does not perform the source operation. Validate the closed schema Plans/runtime_artifact_restore_point.schema.json (pm.runtime_artifact.restore_point.schema.v1) and current producer/read permission before commit. Project root edition only: nonempty payload.project_id must equal the EventRecord 2.0.0 project_id, scope_kind=project; artifact_type=restore_point, schema_id=pm.runtime_artifact.restore_point.schema.v1. All run/attempt/thread/node/provider/usage refs must resolve to that same owning Project and original source; absent optional refs never inherit focused UI identity. Restore-point run_id/attempt_id remain optional attribution; type_payload.restore_point_id is primary and type_payload.project_id equals the envelope Project. Preserve exact source_thread_id/source_branch_id/source_message_id, record_ref and immutable record_sha256 joins to the Chat-owned rp record. safe_point_id remains lineage only. Application successor definitions in CV-366/SP-349/351/352 are separate source/key graphs and are not written into this Project edition; this draft changes none of them.
Newly authored observation identity under DL-045 explicitly completes RAP-054's unfinished four-member recommendation for this lifecycle-changing family only. The four-member tuple [event_type, project_id, artifact_id, schema_id] remains the stable artifact grouping identity, with one unchanged artifact_id and primary type_payload.restore_point_id. Event identity additionally binds the original owner observation revision in EventRecord.producer_sequence_id. idempotency_key is "ra-observation1:" plus lowercase SHA-256 of the five-member tuple [event_type, project_id, artifact_id, schema_id, decimal(producer_sequence_id)], each exact UTF-8 member prefixed with its uint32 big-endian byte length; decimal is a nonnegative integer with no leading zero except "0". EventRecord.event_id is allocated once by Storage on first accepted append. Only sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc are Storage assignments; occurred_at_utc preserves the original producer-authored payload.created_at_utc.
Observation revisions are source-backed technical ordinals, not new point versions or artifact rows. Under the actual append-writer/selection fence, the owner reads the complete verified SP-278 history for this Project/artifact, authenticates the previous observation and its SP-286 full-value first receipt, and validates the current canonical rp/source snapshot through the existing Chat/Storage authority. First revision is 0 with parent_event_id=null; each later accepted lifecycle observation is exactly predecessor revision+1 with parent_event_id equal to that original observation's event_id. Correlation stays the four-member ra1 grouping key. Reject a missing/gapped predecessor, changed point/artifact association, invalid source/hash/Project, unsupported source proof, stale snapshot or parallel stale predecessor; no ordinal is reconstructed from timestamps or payload hashes. Recheck source and predecessor under the same fence before append. No new stored counter or pending request is introduced: committed observations and original receipts are the durable ordinal custody.

No borrowing restore_point.created membership or manufacturing missing capture/companion/custody is permitted.

A later authentic source observation uses the next ordinal while keeping the same point/artifact identity. The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. A schema/source row is not an append or event-checkpoint grant. settings.layer.changed is application-only; normal chat/history/run/tool/Usage/recovery/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule/attention/layout app variants are application_or_project only for their actual admitted writer. Every selected variant must join full original source, commit/append/first-receipt, canonical or derived read/checkpoint, backup/restore and retention. New approval.chat_tool_requested/resolved payloads are thread/tool/target bound, distinct from Project Orchestrator node approval events. Wizard handoff, PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/WorkNode/gates and frozen Workflow/certified sources stay Project-only. Unknown/missing source, version or family is unavailable/quarantined; a registry or all-true fixture boolean cannot admit native writes. Existing notebook/plugin/auth/pause/scheduler candidate/non-emitting dispositions remain until their own complete admission. goal.paused/resumed or any other required unregistered semantic name cannot emit by inference; missing_event_registration is preserved. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.

for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.

claim_audit.text:
The frozen application tables attached to this unit define selected versioned siblings, never an in-place relaxation of a Project codec. Existing Project resource bytes, schema IDs/versions, original accepted-source/hash domains, source/cancel/certification banks and replay readers remain exact. Current compatibility $refs may be added in non-frozen aggregate companions, but never replace an immutable historical resource or rebind an old literal URI to new contents. New app logical IDs use .application.v1 and 1.0.0; shared WorkflowScopeV2 and the thread facade editions are explicit v2 exceptions. The Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contracts.schema.json and Plans/assistant_plan_runtime_contract_fixtures.json pair was created with original Project definitions under their own exact identities and references to the new app definitions, never a duplicate Plan engine.
Hash domains are frozen separately from payload-store addressing and physical codecs. New application semantic hashes use pm.application.semantic_hash.v1: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over UTF-8 domain prefix "pm.application.semantic_hash.v1\0" + exact closed kind + "\0" + RFC8785 canonical JSON of a lossless typed tree. The typed tree is ["null"], ["bool",value], ["string",exact Unicode scalar string], ["int",canonical signed base-10 integer string with no +/leading zero/-0], ["float64",sixteen lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE754 finite value], ["array",ordered typed children] or ["object",[[exact key,typed value],...]] with keys in unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate keys, non-scalar Unicode, NaN/infinity and unknown kinds reject; strings are never normalized/trimmed. This retains arbitrary exact integer identity without coercing values to floating point. Physical records still use their declared numeric types.
Closed semantic kinds are goal_body_currentness, goal_objective_revision, accepted_source, operation_intent, thread_preview, schedule_target, conversion_manifest and source_graph. Each preimage is a closed object: schema_id/schema_version of the selected semantic record, WorkflowScopeV2, the complete semantic record and purpose-specific immutable identity. goal_body_currentness uses the exact eleven-field Goal body with only currentness_hash omitted, plus scope; objective revision hashes its full selected revision including source body link. operation_intent includes command/owner interface, exact actor/target/input/source commitments, expected revisions/Stop/permission/writer generations and idempotency identity; thread_preview includes the full redacted CV-365 preview including expiry. schedule_target includes actual target version/hash/topology/team or exact message text/attachments/destination/time/runtime snapshots. conversion_manifest covers the entire CV-367 manifest excluding only its self-hash. source_graph covers the complete resource/method/graph manifest excluding only graph_sha256. A source hash authenticates bytes only; accepted-source authority still requires its genuine original owner joins.
App physical codec pm.application.physical_messagepack.v1 is deterministic MessagePack of the complete closed wrapper: maps in unsigned UTF-8 key order, minimal integer widths (positive values use unsigned encodings), exact UTF-8 strings without normalization, declared binary as MessagePack binary, finite floats as IEEE754 binary64, arrays in semantic order, no duplicate keys, trailing data or nonminimal encoding. SHA-256 of those exact encoded wrapper bytes is physical_record_sha256, never body currentness/source/semantic digest. Original Project MessagePack/JSON codecs are unchanged. CV-339/SP-286 shared append/wire/full-value commitments stay their own exact domains; SP-337 BLAKE3 payload IDs and immutable binary bytes are not converted to SHA-256 or re-encoded through JSON.
App producer idempotency keys incorporate actual server_id and original owner operation identity as application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)}; the existing storage lifetime tuple remains (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) and app-root-global event_id remains unchanged. Every optional effect uses an exact declared operation component before hashing; no retry timestamp/focus can remint an original source. Same identity/same semantic digest returns the original result; different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe is dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Reversible Project partitions keep Storage’s project~base64url rule, never a new project:hex scheme.
The attached table is the closed event/app-source selection policy. Its CompactionCompletionApplicationV1 shape and source are non-emitting candidates only: context.compaction.completed remains project_only, DL-300 admits no app edition, and missing_event_registration persists until separate Event Authority admission and complete owner adoption. A schema/source row is not an append or event-checkpoint grant. settings.layer.changed is application-only; normal chat/history/run/tool/Usage/recovery/Goal/Crew/Plan/schedule/attention/layout app variants are application_or_project only for their actual admitted writer. Every selected variant must join full original source, commit/append/first-receipt, canonical or derived read/checkpoint, backup/restore and retention. New approval.chat_tool_requested/resolved payloads are thread/tool/target bound, distinct from Project Orchestrator node approval events. Wizard handoff, PRD/PlanningRun/NamedPlan/WorkNode/gates and frozen Workflow/certified sources stay Project-only. Unknown/missing source, version or family is unavailable/quarantined; a registry or all-true fixture boolean cannot admit native writes. Existing notebook/plugin/auth/pause/scheduler candidate/non-emitting dispositions remain until their own complete admission. goal.paused/resumed or any other required unregistered semantic name cannot emit by inference; missing_event_registration is preserved. App support is an accepted requirement, while native availability and exact source adoption remain evidence-bounded.
The developer-session resources are separately selected in Plans/developer_session_application_contracts.schema.json: DebugSessionRecordApplicationV1 and EvalSessionRecordApplicationV1 plus their physical wrappers. OriginalDebugSessionSource and OriginalEvalSessionSource select owner.debug.session.application@1.0.0 and owner.eval.session.application@1.0.0 under the existing DebugSessionBroker/EvalSessionBroker. The two added ordered source graphs cover original intent, pending/lease/Stop fence, commit, receipt/result/read, coherent backup and retention; both stay specified_unimplemented. Browser sources/profile/page/controller records belong only to the browser owner. Project dev_session_record/eval_session_record codecs and sources retain exact bytes.
CV-740 explicitly selects the separate header-bearing app board V2 whole source/message/wrapper graph
for current posts and V2 original-message consumers. The frozen V1 table remains exact for supported
historical V1 selection; this narrow successor never rebinds a frozen literal URI or Project codec.
CV-1100 and SP-1101 govern exact input and authenticated original-recipe dispatch; this unit retains its typed semantic tree, app float64/binary physical profile, closed kinds, exact prefixes and original Project codecs.

Crash discards volatile prepared/event/receipt caches; recovery restores them only from the durable phase and authoritative issued full value plus unchanged first receipt. After issuance, retained duplicate resolution uses issued EventRecord/receipt custody independently of disposed original command, approval or mutation controls, and performs no domain reexecution. A body-dependent read can still be unavailable under its own owner policy.

Newly authored Storage bindings only for server.endpoint_changed@1.0.0, prepared without admission. SRV-1418/CV-1418 own the exact semantic contract. Three closed independently keyed values live in Plans/storage_value_registry.json: w3e_server_endpoint_changed_custody, w3e_server_endpoint_changed_history and w3e_server_endpoint_changed_checkpoint. Historical preparation snapshot (2026-11-19, received 2bda6aeed0): «Current writes remain missing_event_registration»; retention_policy_ref=RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE@1.0.0 (DL-453, E-CARDS-3 item 1.a, option A), kept permanently, application editions only, with no age or count expiry and no new count allowance; storage pressure refuses new history writes, and explicit application data deletion follows its existing authorized rules. Deleting the described object does not remove this separate history or keep the deleted content. The custody, history and checkpoint values below inherit this assignment; their Storage registry rows carry it at the batch-3 rebase, when every decided policy object is on the lane. Custody in canonical redb uses w3e_server_endpoint_changed_custody.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{scope_partition}:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)} and Plans/event_payloads/w3e/server_endpoint_changed.schema.json#/$defs/custody. It retains original intent, complete before/after source refs, original owner result, semantic input, stable event identity/digest and nullable first append-result ref. pending_append becomes settled only with actual CV-339 full-value original result; source/receipt ambiguity becomes recovery_required. It is not reconstructed from the event. Domain authority remains ServerCatalogService.endpoint_commit@1.0.0; Storage owns atomic persistence only.
Derived history in redb projections uses w3e_server_endpoint_changed_history.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{scope_partition}:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(owner_operation_id)} and Plans/event_payloads/w3e/server_endpoint_changed.schema.json#/$defs/history. Its only producer is projector.w3e.server_endpoint_changed.history@1.0.0; reader.w3e.server_endpoint_changed.history@1.0.0 serves Server endpoint list/Details and Remote Access endpoint association under source/access/deletion/withdrawal checks. It contains only the original event/custody/payload references, canonical sequence and publication generation, no new live domain state.
The exact checkpoint in derived redb checkpoints is w3e_server_endpoint_changed_checkpoint.v1:{hex(storage_instance_id)}:{scope_partition}:{hex(server_id)} and Plans/event_payloads/w3e/server_endpoint_changed.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint. Adopt SP-278 reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0 by name for actual all-partition source completeness, then exact-family/scope/writer filtering. Both the projection-generation pointer and exact checkpoint advance with changed rows under prior-value CAS in one write transaction. Persist the nine-field durable generic_read_token (DL-076), never redb_snapshot_id; join a fresh live read snapshot for validation. Checkpoints cannot publish the generic index or select CURRENT. Inclusive restart verifies last_examined_cursor frame identity/end offset; no cursor regression or unsupported-source skip. Withdrawal fences source/reader and invalidates publication; verified shadow rebuild swaps atomically without source mutation.
Adopt SP-286 and CV-339 first-AppendReceipt and full-value v2 custody, SP-236 physical bytes and SP-337 large-body addressing by name. Each encoded value has the SP-340 maximum 16384 bytes in its named canonical/derived file and projects_and_sources storage group; measure the entire stored wrapper. Every larger source, owner result, semantic input, payload or token graph is externalized with SP-337 immutable BLAKE3 id/size/media type evidence before its referencing acknowledgement. A large checkpoint uses its closed body_inline=null/body_ref SP-337 route; a small one uses body_inline with body_ref=null. Resolve and validate the complete immutable checkpoint_body under the same token/CAS/source fence. If even a ref-only wrapper exceeds its bound, refuse; never truncate, base64-wrap or silently enlarge the limit. Original source schema/recipe and access proofs travel with the referenced source bytes. A complete canonical backup includes source/pending/terminal, referenced payload closure, EventRecord group/first result and original dedupe; unresolved restore fences current publication. Derived values are omitted and rebuilt from verified current survivors, preserving gaps and historical schemas. Pending event retention is no purge authority; holds and source/receipt dependencies remain independent. No fresh Store version, native runtime, admission or lifetime is invented.

Adopt CV-317 EventRecord and CV-339/SP-286 full-value receipt custody by name; do not duplicate the envelope. Required exact fields are schema_id, schema_version, scope_kind, project_id, server_id, owner_operation_id, source_custody_ref, source_evidence_ref, server_endpoint_id, expected_fingerprint, observed_fingerprint, detection_id, mismatch_evidence_ref. Externalized SP-337 body dispatch validates the resolved complete payload against this same schema; do not validate the reference string as the object or require payload_ref=null. All $refs resolve eagerly. Schema integer domains are inherited, exact Python/JSON boolean-number types are distinct, and identifier/digest strings require full consumption without trailing LF. Timestamps, where inherited through source/token schemas, use their owner-selected shared profile; write no local validator. No schema or fixture admits this family. retention_policy_ref=RP-OPERATIONAL-SECURITY-APPLICATION-2555D@1.0.0 (DL-455, E-CARDS-3 item 3.a, option A), application editions only, kept seven years (220,752,000 seconds) from the original saved change, never restarted by retry, reprocessing or restore, in the one separate 2,000,000-entry application allowance app:operational_security (fail_closed overflow, hold eligible; only expired unprotected entries are removed). The policy object is defined on main (Plans/storage-plan.md third-sitting retention assignments) and arrives on this lane with the batch-3 rebase. Phase 2 (2026-11-13) runs the executable synthetic oracles of this family in scripts/pm_w3e_event_oracles.py; every refusal is one named single-predicate row of a generated Method B guard table (scripts/pm_w3e_table_*.py) proved by the gated shared scripts/pm_guard_isolation.py through scripts/pm-w3e-guard-proof.py, and rows no input can refuse first stay alone in their own table with a written proof. Numbers use the shared CV-1100/SP-1100 calls and timestamps the shared CV-1101 date_time with the owner profile of each field. Identity: owner_operation_id is family-operation@1: plus lowercase SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 bytes "pm.w3e.owner_fact.v1\0" + hex(owner_method) + "\0" + hex(original_operation_id) + "\0" + hex(immutable_fact_id). hex is lowercase hexadecimal of exact UTF-8 bytes, no normalization; immutable_fact_id is the original accepted phase/journal entry ID, observation ID, detection ID or receipt fact, allocated once and durably preserved before use. Multiple facts in one operation use distinct original fact IDs, never clock/focus or retry counters. event_id is w3e@1: plus lowercase SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 bytes "pm.event.server.identity_mismatch_detected.identity.v1\0" + scope_partition + "\0" + hex(server_id) + "\0" + hex(owner_operation_id). No numeric or timestamp value is serialized by this string-only identity recipe.

Historical originals use their authenticated original schema/recipe even after live trust, state, route, source visibility or stricter format rules change, subject to current access/deletion/withdrawal checks. Replay is only filtered derived history; it never dispatches a command, network test, notification, pairing, revocation, backup, restore, route activation, billing, timer or canonical write.

Original source bodies, receipts and secrets keep their independent existing rules. A missing member is disclosed, history stays unavailable and current effects stay fenced; restore never grants current authority.

A permitted historical-only reader must be separately bound to retained exact bytes and current access/deletion fences. Rebuild only after a complete admitted replacement source/generation is verified; atomic publication cannot reinterpret old payloads or reissue domain work. Source retention/deletion authority remains independent.
